name: Data reporting & presenting results
description: Chart types, trend and number language, statistics, KPIs and the phrases you need to walk a meeting through data analysis results.

words.definition: A picture that shows data, such as bars, lines or slices, so people can see patterns quickly.

examples.en: This chart shows our monthly active users over the last twelve months.
examples.zh: 这张图表展示了过去十二个月的月活跃用户数。

words.note: chart 和 graph 在口语里基本通用；商务场合（尤其 Excel/PowerPoint）多说 chart。

words.definition: A diagram that shows how values change or relate, usually with lines or points plotted against two axes.

examples.en: If you look at the graph, the line starts to flatten out in May.
examples.zh: 看这张图，曲线从五月开始趋于平缓。

words.note: graph 更偏指有坐标轴的折线图/函数图；饼图一般不叫 graph，叫 pie chart。

words.definition: A chart that joins data points with a line, usually to show how something changes over time.

examples.en: I've used a line chart here because we're looking at the trend over time.
examples.zh: 这里我用折线图，因为我们看的是随时间变化的趋势。

examples.en: The orange line is this year and the grey line is last year.
examples.zh: 橙色的线是今年，灰色的线是去年。

words.note: 也叫 line graph，两者通用。

words.definition: A chart that compares categories using rectangular bars whose length shows the value.

examples.en: This bar chart compares ticket volumes across our five support teams.
examples.zh: 这个柱状图比较了五个支持团队的工单量。

words.note: 英式/新西兰日常说 bar chart 时，竖的、横的都可以；Excel 里把竖的叫 column chart，横的才叫 bar chart。

words.definition: A bar chart with vertical bars; the name Excel and PowerPoint use for upright bars.

examples.en: I'll switch this to a column chart so the months run along the bottom.
examples.zh: 我把它换成柱形图，这样月份就沿着底部排列。

words.note: column = 竖着的柱子（柱形图）；bar = 横着的条（条形图）。口语里很多人把两者都叫 bar chart。

words.definition: A bar chart with bars running left to right, useful when category names are long.

examples.en: I've used a horizontal bar chart because the product names are quite long.
examples.zh: 我用了横向条形图，因为产品名称比较长。

words.note: 排行榜（Top 10）通常用横向条形图，从大到小排序。

words.definition: A bar chart where each bar is split into coloured parts that add up to the total.

examples.en: In this stacked bar chart, each colour is a region, and the full bar is total revenue.
examples.zh: 在这张堆积柱形图里，每种颜色代表一个地区，整根柱子是总收入。

words.note: 竖向的也可叫 stacked column chart。

words.definition: A stacked chart where every column is the same height and each part shows its share of the total.

examples.en: This 100% stacked column chart shows the mix of mobile and desktop traffic each month.
examples.zh: 这张百分比堆积柱形图展示了每月移动端和桌面端流量的构成。

words.note: 读作 a hundred percent stacked column chart；看的是占比变化，不是总量变化。

words.zh: 簇状柱形图；分组柱状图
words.definition: A bar chart that puts bars for different series side by side within each category.

examples.en: The clustered bar chart puts this year and last year side by side for each quarter.
examples.zh: 簇状柱形图把每个季度的今年和去年并排放在一起。

words.note: 也叫 grouped bar chart；Excel 里叫 clustered column / clustered bar。

words.definition: A circle divided into slices, where each slice shows a category's share of the whole.

examples.en: The pie chart shows that almost half of our tickets come from password resets.
examples.zh: 饼图显示我们将近一半的工单来自密码重置。

words.note: 饼图只适合少量分类（一般不超过五六个），各部分加起来要等于100%。

words.definition: A pie chart with a hole in the middle, often with the total written in the centre.

examples.en: The doughnut chart has the total number of users in the middle.
examples.zh: 环形图中间写着用户总数。

words.note: 美式拼写 donut chart；Excel 里叫 Doughnut。

words.definition: A chart that shows how values are spread by counting how many fall into each range, or bin.

examples.en: This histogram shows the distribution of page load times.
examples.zh: 这张直方图展示了页面加载时间的分布。

examples.en: Most requests fall in the 200 to 400 millisecond range.
examples.zh: 大部分请求落在200到400毫秒之间。

words.note: 直方图横轴是连续的数值区间（柱子之间没有空隙）；柱状图横轴是分类。

words.definition: A chart that plots each item as a dot using two numeric values, to show whether they are related.

examples.en: Each dot on this scatter plot is a customer: spend on one axis, tickets raised on the other.
examples.zh: 这张散点图上每个点是一个客户：一个轴是消费额，另一个轴是提交的工单数。

words.note: 也说 scatter chart、scatter graph、scattergram。

words.definition: A scatter plot where the size of each bubble shows a third value.

examples.en: In the bubble chart, the bigger the bubble, the more revenue that client brings in.
examples.zh: 在气泡图里，气泡越大，该客户带来的收入越多。

words.definition: A line chart with the space under the line filled in with colour to emphasise volume.

examples.en: The area chart makes it easy to see how total storage has grown.
examples.zh: 面积图让人很容易看出总存储量是如何增长的。

words.definition: An area chart where several series are piled on top of each other to show parts of a total over time.

examples.en: The stacked area chart shows that most of the growth came from the cloud segment.
examples.zh: 堆积面积图显示大部分增长来自云业务板块。

words.definition: A chart showing the median, quartiles and spread of data as a box with lines (whiskers) on each side.

examples.en: The box plot shows that Team B's resolution times are much more spread out.
examples.zh: 箱线图显示B团队的解决时间分散得多。

words.note: 也叫 box-and-whisker plot（盒须图）。箱子中间的线是中位数，箱子两端是上下四分位数。

words.definition: A grid where colour intensity shows the size of each value, so hot spots stand out.

examples.en: The heat map shows that most logins happen on weekday mornings.
examples.zh: 热力图显示大部分登录发生在工作日上午。

words.note: 也常写成一个词 heatmap。

words.definition: A chart that shows how a starting value moves to an ending value through a series of increases and decreases.

examples.en: This waterfall chart walks us from last year's profit to this year's, step by step.
examples.zh: 这张瀑布图一步步展示了从去年利润到今年利润的变化。

words.note: 常用于 bridge（利润桥/差异分析），也叫 bridge chart。

words.definition: A chart showing how many people are left at each stage of a process, such as visit, sign-up and purchase.

examples.en: The funnel chart shows we lose most users between sign-up and first purchase.
examples.zh: 漏斗图显示我们在注册到首次购买之间流失的用户最多。

words.definition: A bar chart of a project schedule, with each task shown as a bar along a timeline.

examples.en: The Gantt chart shows the data migration finishing in late March.
examples.zh: 甘特图显示数据迁移将在三月下旬完成。

words.definition: A chart that shows parts of a whole as nested rectangles, sized by value.

examples.en: In this treemap, the biggest rectangle is compute, which is most of our cloud spend.
examples.zh: 在这张矩形树图里，最大的矩形是计算资源，占了我们云支出的大部分。

words.definition: A tiny line chart, usually inside a table cell, that shows a trend without axes or labels.

examples.en: The sparklines in the last column give you the twelve-month trend for each metric.
examples.zh: 最后一列的迷你图展示了每个指标十二个月的趋势。

words.definition: A chart that combines two chart types, such as columns for volume and a line for a rate.

examples.en: This combo chart shows sales as columns and conversion rate as a line.
examples.zh: 这张组合图用柱子表示销售额，用折线表示转化率。

words.note: 也说 combination chart。

words.definition: A chart with a second vertical axis on the right, so two measures with different scales can share one chart.

examples.en: It's a dual-axis chart, so revenue is on the left axis and margin is on the right.
examples.zh: 这是双轴图，收入看左轴，利润率看右轴。

words.note: 双轴图容易误导，讲的时候要说清楚哪条线对应哪个轴。

words.definition: Data arranged in rows and columns.

examples.en: I've put the exact numbers in the table at the bottom of the slide.
examples.zh: 我把具体数字放在了幻灯片底部的表格里。

words.definition: A spreadsheet table that summarises data by grouping it, for example total sales by region and month.

examples.en: I built a quick pivot table to break the tickets down by priority.
examples.zh: 我做了一个数据透视表，按优先级拆分了工单。

words.definition: A screen that shows several key charts and numbers together, often updated automatically.

examples.en: All of these numbers are live on the Power BI dashboard.
examples.zh: 这些数字在 Power BI 看板上都是实时的。

words.definition: A box on a dashboard showing one key number, often with its change and a coloured arrow.

examples.en: The KPI tiles across the top show this month's numbers against target.
examples.zh: 顶部的指标卡显示本月数字与目标的对比。

words.note: 也叫 KPI card、scorecard（Looker Studio 里叫 scorecard）、big number。

words.zh: 分级统计地图（按区域着色）
words.definition: A map where each region is shaded by its value, darker for higher numbers.

examples.en: On the choropleth map, Auckland and Canterbury are the darkest regions.
examples.zh: 在这张分级统计地图上，奥克兰和坎特伯雷颜色最深。

words.note: 日常也就说 map 或 filled map（Power BI 叫 filled map）。

words.definition: A chart with several axes coming out from the centre, used to compare items across many measures.

examples.en: The radar chart compares the three vendors across six criteria.
examples.zh: 雷达图在六项标准上比较了三家供应商。

words.note: 也叫 spider chart（蜘蛛图）。

words.definition: A bar chart sorted from largest to smallest, with a line showing the cumulative percentage.

examples.en: The Pareto chart shows that three error types cause about 80% of the outages.
examples.zh: 帕累托图显示三种错误类型造成了约80%的故障。

words.definition: A line chart with upper and lower limits, used to see whether a process is stable or out of control.

examples.en: On the control chart, these two points fall outside the upper limit.
examples.zh: 在控制图上，这两个点超出了上控制限。

words.definition: A flow diagram where the width of each band shows how much moves from one stage to another.

examples.en: The Sankey diagram shows where our website traffic goes after the home page.
examples.zh: 桑基图展示了网站流量离开首页后的去向。

words.definition: A compact bar showing an actual value against a target marker and shaded performance bands.

examples.en: Each bullet chart shows the actual figure as a bar and the target as a small vertical line.
examples.zh: 每个子弹图用横条表示实际值，用小竖线表示目标值。

words.note: 也叫 bullet graph。

words.definition: A grid of small charts with the same axes, one for each category, so they can be compared at a glance.

examples.en: Instead of one busy chart, I've used small multiples: one small line chart per region.
examples.zh: 我没有用一张拥挤的图，而是用了小多图：每个地区一个小折线图。

words.definition: Showing data as charts, maps or other pictures so people can understand it.

examples.en: Good data visualisation means the audience gets the point in five seconds.
examples.zh: 好的数据可视化能让听众五秒内抓住重点。

words.note: 美式拼写 visualization；口语常缩写为 data viz（读 VIZ）。

words.definition: A designed graphic that combines charts, icons and short text to tell a story with data.

examples.en: Marketing turned our survey results into an infographic for the newsletter.
examples.zh: 市场部把我们的调查结果做成了信息图，放进了简报。

words.definition: The horizontal line along the bottom of a chart, often showing time or categories.

examples.en: Along the x-axis we have the months, from July to June.
examples.zh: 横轴是月份，从七月到次年六月。

words.note: axis 复数是 axes（读 AK-seez）。

words.definition: The vertical line on the left of a chart, usually showing the values being measured.

examples.en: The y-axis shows the number of incidents per week.
examples.zh: 纵轴表示每周的事件数量。

words.definition: The axis that runs left to right across the bottom of a chart; another name for the x-axis.

examples.en: Time runs along the horizontal axis.
examples.zh: 时间沿着水平轴排列。

words.definition: The axis that runs up the side of a chart; another name for the y-axis.

examples.en: On the vertical axis we have revenue in millions of dollars.
examples.zh: 纵轴是收入，单位是百万元。

words.definition: A second value axis, usually on the right-hand side, used for a measure with a different scale.

examples.en: The conversion rate uses the secondary axis on the right.
examples.zh: 转化率用的是右边的次坐标轴。

words.note: 也说 right-hand axis；左边的叫 primary axis（主坐标轴）。

words.zh: 坐标轴标签；坐标轴标题
words.definition: The text next to an axis saying what it measures and in what unit.

examples.en: Sorry, the axis label is missing: this is response time in seconds.
examples.zh: 抱歉，坐标轴标题漏了：这是以秒为单位的响应时间。

words.definition: The range and spacing of numbers along an axis.

examples.en: Note that the two charts use different scales.
examples.zh: 请注意这两张图用的刻度不一样。

words.definition: An axis where each step multiplies the value, for example 1, 10, 100, 1,000, used when numbers vary hugely.

examples.en: I've put this on a log scale, otherwise the smaller customers would be invisible.
examples.zh: 我把它改成了对数刻度，不然小客户就完全看不见了。

words.note: 全称 logarithmic scale（读 log-uh-RITH-mik）。普通刻度叫 linear scale（线性刻度）。

words.zh: 截断的坐标轴（不从0开始）
words.definition: A value axis that does not start at zero, which can make small changes look big.

examples.en: Be careful: the y-axis starts at 90%, so the drop looks bigger than it is.
examples.zh: 注意：纵轴从90%开始，所以下降看起来比实际大。

words.note: 讲图时主动说 the axis doesn't start at zero，能显得专业、诚实。

words.definition: A small line on an axis that marks a value or interval.

examples.en: Each tick mark on the x-axis is one week.
examples.zh: 横轴上每个刻度代表一周。

words.note: 口语常简称 tick。

words.definition: A faint line across the chart area that helps the eye read values.

examples.en: I've removed the gridlines to make the chart cleaner.
examples.zh: 我去掉了网格线，让图表更简洁。

words.definition: The key that explains what each colour, line or symbol in a chart means.

examples.en: As the legend shows, the dark blue bars are actuals and the light blue bars are budget.
examples.zh: 如图例所示，深蓝色柱子是实际数，浅蓝色柱子是预算。

words.note: 也可以说 key（The key is at the top right）。

words.definition: A single value shown on a chart, such as one dot or one point on a line.

examples.en: Each data point is one day's total.
examples.zh: 每个数据点是一天的总数。

words.definition: The number written directly on or next to a bar, slice or point.

examples.en: I've added data labels so you don't have to read values off the axis.
examples.zh: 我加了数据标签，这样大家不用对着坐标轴读数。

words.definition: One set of related values plotted together, such as one line or one colour of bars.

examples.en: There are three series on this chart: Auckland, Wellington and Christchurch.
examples.zh: 这张图上有三个数据系列：奥克兰、惠灵顿和基督城。

words.note: series 单复数同形：one series, two series。

words.definition: One of the groups being compared in a chart, such as a product, team or region.

examples.en: The 'Other' category combines everything under 2%.
examples.zh: “其他”类别合并了所有占比低于2%的项目。

words.definition: One rectangle in a bar or column chart.

examples.en: The tallest bar is December, which is our peak season.
examples.zh: 最高的柱子是十二月，是我们的旺季。

words.definition: One piece of a pie or doughnut chart.

examples.en: The biggest slice is licensing, at 42% of total cost.
examples.zh: 最大的扇区是许可费，占总成本的42%。

words.definition: A straight or smooth line added to a chart to show the general direction of the data.

examples.en: If you look at the trend line, the overall direction is still upward.
examples.zh: 看趋势线，整体方向仍然是向上的。

words.note: Excel 里写作 trendline（一个词）。

words.definition: The straight line that best matches the pattern of points on a scatter plot.

examples.en: The line of best fit slopes upward, so more training hours go with higher scores.
examples.zh: 最佳拟合线向上倾斜，说明培训时长越多，分数越高。

words.definition: A short note added to a chart to explain a specific point or event.

examples.en: I've added an annotation where the new pricing went live.
examples.zh: 我在新定价上线的位置加了一个标注。

words.definition: A highlighted label or box on a slide that draws attention to one number or point.

examples.en: The callout on the right highlights the 12% drop in March.
examples.zh: 右边的标注框突出显示了三月下降12%。

words.definition: Using colours consistently to show meaning, such as red for below target and green for on target.

examples.en: The colour coding is the same on every slide: green is on track, red is at risk.
examples.zh: 每页的颜色编码都一样：绿色表示正常，红色表示有风险。

words.note: 美式拼写 color coding。

words.definition: A horizontal or vertical line marking an important value, such as an average or a date.

examples.en: The dotted reference line is the twelve-month average.
examples.zh: 那条点状参考线是十二个月的平均值。

words.definition: A line across a chart showing the goal, so you can see which values are above or below it.

examples.en: Everything above the red target line met the SLA.
examples.zh: 红色目标线以上的都达到了服务等级协议。

words.definition: A small line on a bar or point showing the range of uncertainty around the value.

examples.en: The error bars overlap, so we can't say the two groups are really different.
examples.zh: 误差线有重叠，所以我们不能说这两组真的有差异。

words.definition: The heading of a chart that says what it shows.

examples.en: I like to use the chart title to state the main finding, not just the topic.
examples.zh: 我喜欢用图表标题直接写出主要结论，而不只是写主题。

words.definition: A small note at the bottom of a slide or chart giving sources, definitions or caveats.

examples.en: The footnote explains that the figures exclude GST.
examples.zh: 脚注说明这些数字不含消费税。

words.definition: A small box that appears when you hover over part of an interactive chart, showing the exact values.

examples.en: If you hover over any point, the tooltip shows the exact number.
examples.zh: 把鼠标悬停在任意一个点上，悬停提示会显示具体数字。

words.definition: A smooth bending line on a chart.

examples.en: The curve gets steeper after the launch.
examples.zh: 上线之后曲线变得更陡了。

words.definition: A line made of short dashes, often used for forecasts, targets or projections.

examples.en: The solid line is actuals and the dashed line is our forecast.
examples.zh: 实线是实际数，虚线是我们的预测。

words.note: dashed line 是短划线组成的虚线；dotted line 是点组成的点线；solid line 是实线。

words.definition: A shaded band on a chart that marks a period or range, such as a holiday or a forecast range.

examples.en: The shaded area marks the Christmas shutdown period.
examples.zh: 阴影区域标出了圣诞停工期。

words.definition: One of four sections of a chart created by splitting it with a horizontal and a vertical line.

examples.en: The customers in the top-right quadrant are high value and highly engaged.
examples.zh: 右上象限的客户价值高、活跃度也高。

words.definition: In a box plot, a line extending from the box to show the range of most of the data.

examples.en: The long upper whisker shows a few very slow requests.
examples.zh: 上方很长的须说明有少数请求非常慢。

words.definition: One range of values in a histogram, such as 0 to 100 milliseconds.

examples.en: I've used 50-millisecond bins for this histogram.
examples.zh: 这个直方图我用了50毫秒一个分组。

words.note: bin width 叫组距；bin 太宽会掩盖细节，太窄会显得很乱。

words.definition: The measure a number is expressed in, such as dollars, hours or users.

examples.en: Just to be clear on the units, these figures are in thousands of dollars.
examples.zh: 先说明一下单位，这些数字以千元为单位。

words.definition: Grow by a certain amount; the number after 'by' is the size of the change.

examples.en: Revenue increased by 4% compared with last quarter.
examples.zh: 收入比上季度增长了4%。

examples.en: Headcount increased by 12 people this year.
examples.zh: 今年人数增加了12人。

words.note: increase BY 4% = 增长了4%（幅度）；increase TO 4% = 增长到4%（结果）。中文“增长4%”一般是 by。

words.definition: Grow until reaching a certain level; the number after 'to' is the new value.

examples.en: The churn rate increased to 4% in March.
examples.zh: 三月的流失率上升到了4%。

words.note: to 后面是新的数值；如果从3%到4%，要说 increased to 4%，或 increased by one percentage point。

words.definition: The pattern for giving the old value and the new value of a change.

examples.en: Average response time fell from 3.2 seconds to 1.8 seconds.
examples.zh: 平均响应时间从3.2秒降到了1.8秒。

examples.en: Monthly users went from 40,000 to just over 52,000.
examples.zh: 月活用户从4万增加到5.2万多一点。

words.note: 讲图时最清楚的说法：先说 from 旧值 to 新值，再补一句幅度（that's an increase of 30%）。

words.definition: A noun phrase for the size of a rise, as in 'an increase of 4%'.

examples.en: That's an increase of 15% on the same period last year.
examples.zh: 这比去年同期增长了15%。

words.note: 名词用 of：an increase of 4%、a drop of 2 points；动词用 by：increased by 4%。注意 increase on last year 的 on = 相比。

words.definition: A short, spoken way to say something has increased by 4%.

examples.en: Sales are up 4% on last month.
examples.zh: 销售额比上个月增长了4%。

examples.en: Logins were up 10% year on year.
examples.zh: 登录次数同比增长了10%。

words.note: up 4% = increased by 4% = a 4% increase，三种说法意思一样；口头汇报最常用 up / down。

words.definition: A short, spoken way to say something has decreased by 4%.

examples.en: Support tickets are down 18% since we launched the new help centre.
examples.zh: 自从上线新的帮助中心，支持工单下降了18%。

words.note: 比较对象用 on 或 compared with：down 4% on last year。

words.definition: A noun phrase for an increase where the size comes first, before 'rise', 'increase' or 'drop'.

examples.en: We saw a 4% rise in active users after the update.
examples.zh: 更新后活跃用户增长了4%。

words.note: 数字放前面时做形容词：a 4% rise / a two-point drop；放后面要用 of：a rise of 4%。

words.definition: The simple difference between two percentages, for example from 10% to 12% is two percentage points.

examples.en: Conversion went from 10% to 12%, which is up two percentage points, or a 20% relative increase.
examples.zh: 转化率从10%升到12%，上升了两个百分点，相对增长20%。

words.note: 10%→12%：是“上升2个百分点（percentage points）”，也是“相对增长20%”；不能说 up 2%，那会让人误解。口语常简称 points：up two points。

words.definition: Out of every hundred; used directly after a number, as in 45 percent.

examples.en: About 45 percent of users are on mobile.
examples.zh: 大约45%的用户使用手机。

words.note: 英式/新西兰也写 per cent（两个词）。percent 跟在数字后；没有数字时用 percentage：a high percentage of users。

words.definition: A number expressed as a part of 100, used when no specific number is given.

examples.en: A large percentage of the errors come from one integration.
examples.zh: 很大比例的错误来自同一个集成。

words.note: 不说 a high percent，要说 a high percentage。

words.definition: One hundredth of a percentage point, often used for interest rates and margins.

examples.en: Our margin improved by 30 basis points, from 21.4% to 21.7%.
examples.zh: 我们的利润率提高了30个基点，从21.4%到21.7%。

words.note: 缩写 bp 或 bps（读 bips 或 B-P-S）。100个基点 = 1个百分点。

words.definition: Compared with the previous month.

examples.en: Active users grew 5% month-on-month.
examples.zh: 活跃用户环比增长5%。

examples.en: On a month-on-month basis, costs were flat.
examples.zh: 按环比看，成本持平。

words.note: 缩写 MoM。英式/新西兰说 month-on-month，美式说 month-over-month。“环比”在英语里要说清楚比的是上月、上季度还是上周。

words.definition: Compared with the same period one year earlier.

examples.en: Revenue is up 8% year-on-year.
examples.zh: 收入同比增长8%。

examples.en: Year-on-year growth slowed to 3% in the second quarter.
examples.zh: 第二季度同比增长放缓到3%。

words.note: 缩写 YoY；美式说 year-over-year。“同比”= year-on-year；“环比”= month-on-month / quarter-on-quarter。

words.definition: Compared with the previous quarter.

examples.en: Gross margin was down slightly quarter-on-quarter.
examples.zh: 毛利率季度环比略有下降。

words.note: 缩写 QoQ；美式 quarter-over-quarter。

words.definition: Compared with the previous week.

examples.en: Traffic is up 12% week-on-week, mainly because of the campaign.
examples.zh: 流量周环比增长12%，主要是因为这次推广活动。

words.note: 缩写 WoW（读 W-O-W 或 week on week）；美式 week-over-week。

words.definition: From the start of the year (calendar or financial) until now.

examples.en: Year to date, we've closed 1,240 tickets.
examples.zh: 年初至今，我们已关闭1240张工单。

examples.en: Our YTD spend is tracking slightly under budget.
examples.zh: 我们年初至今的支出略低于预算。

words.note: 缩写 YTD；类似的有 MTD（month to date，本月至今）、QTD（本季度至今）。要说明是自然年还是财年。

words.term: compared with the same period last year
words.definition: Comparing a period with the matching period twelve months earlier.

examples.en: Compared with the same period last year, refunds are down by a third.
examples.zh: 与去年同期相比，退款减少了三分之一。

words.note: 也说 compared to / versus the same period last year；口语可简化为 on last year。

words.definition: The period just before the one being reported, such as last month or last quarter.

examples.en: All the percentages here are compared with the previous period.
examples.zh: 这里所有百分比都是和上期比较的。

words.note: 也说 prior period；报表里常写 vs PP 或 vs prior period。

words.definition: Become twice as large.

examples.en: The number of API calls has doubled since January.
examples.zh: 从一月份到现在，API 调用量翻了一倍。

words.note: doubled = 变成原来的2倍（增长100%）。

words.definition: Become three times as large.

examples.en: Storage costs have almost tripled in two years.
examples.zh: 两年内存储成本几乎涨到了三倍。

words.note: tripled = 变成原来的3倍（增长200%），不是“增长了3倍”的意思，中文翻译要小心。

words.definition: Become half as large, or cut something by 50%.

examples.en: We've halved the average wait time.
examples.zh: 我们把平均等待时间减少了一半。

words.note: 动词 halve，名词 half。fall by half = 减半。

words.definition: Three times as much or as many; used as 'a threefold increase' or 'increase threefold'.

examples.en: We've seen a threefold increase in sign-ups since the free trial launched.
examples.zh: 免费试用上线后，注册量增长到了原来的三倍。

words.note: X-fold（twofold、tenfold）= 变成X倍；正式书面用得多，口语更常说 three times as many。

words.definition: A pattern for comparing size, as in 'three times as many users'.

examples.en: Mobile users raise twice as many tickets as desktop users.
examples.zh: 手机用户提交的工单是桌面用户的两倍。

words.note: 可数用 as many，不可数用 as much。“three times more”有歧义（3倍还是4倍？），汇报时用 three times as many 更清楚。

words.definition: One of three equal parts; about 33%.

examples.en: Roughly a third of our customers use the mobile app every week.
examples.zh: 大约三分之一的客户每周使用手机应用。

words.definition: Two of three equal parts; about 67%.

examples.en: Two-thirds of the delay came from waiting for approvals.
examples.zh: 三分之二的延误来自等待审批。

words.definition: One of four equal parts; 25%.

examples.en: Just under a quarter of tickets were reopened.
examples.zh: 略少于四分之一的工单被重新打开。

words.note: three quarters = 四分之三。注意 a quarter 也可以是“一个季度”，要看上下文。

words.definition: One of two equal parts; 50%.

examples.en: Nearly half of the budget goes on licences.
examples.zh: 将近一半的预算花在许可证上。

words.zh: 五分之一；每五个中有一个
words.definition: A spoken way to give a proportion, such as 20%.

examples.en: One in five new users never logs in again.
examples.zh: 每五个新用户中就有一个再也没有登录过。

words.note: 比百分比更好记，适合用来强调重点：one in three、nine out of ten。

words.definition: Not exactly, but close to the number given.

examples.en: Roughly 60% of the traffic is from New Zealand.
examples.zh: 大约60%的流量来自新西兰。

words.note: roughly、about、around 口语最常用；approximately 更正式。

words.definition: A formal word for close to a number but not exact.

examples.en: The migration will affect approximately 3,000 accounts.
examples.zh: 这次迁移将影响约3000个账户。

words.note: 书面常缩写 approx. 或 ~。

words.definition: Close to; a little more or a little less than.

examples.en: We're seeing around 200 sign-ups a day.
examples.zh: 我们每天大概有200个注册。

words.definition: Slightly less than the number given.

examples.en: Uptime was just under 99.9% this month.
examples.zh: 本月正常运行时间略低于99.9%。

words.note: just under / just below = 稍微低于；just over / just above = 稍微高于。

words.definition: Slightly more than the number given.

examples.en: Just over half of respondents rated us eight or above.
examples.zh: 刚过一半的受访者给我们打了8分及以上。

words.definition: Very close to but not quite reaching the number.

examples.en: We're nearly at our annual target, at 96%.
examples.zh: 我们已经接近年度目标，达到了96%。

words.note: nearly 和 almost 基本同义，都表示“还没达到”。

words.definition: A British-style phrase meaning approximately.

examples.en: The total cost will be in the region of $200,000.
examples.zh: 总成本大约在20万元左右。

words.definition: Compound annual growth rate: the steady yearly growth rate that would take a value from its start to its end over several years.

examples.en: Revenue grew at a CAGR of 12% over the past five years.
examples.zh: 过去五年收入的复合年均增长率为12%。

words.note: 可以念成一个词 KAY-gar，也可以逐个字母读 C-A-G-R。

words.definition: The overall change after adding all increases and subtracting all decreases.

examples.en: We gained 300 customers and lost 120, so the net change is plus 180.
examples.zh: 我们新增300个客户、流失120个，净变化是增加180个。

words.definition: The difference in actual units between two values, such as 50 users or $2,000.

examples.en: In absolute terms it's only 40 tickets, but that's a 25% jump.
examples.zh: 绝对数上只有40张工单，但这是25%的大幅增长。

words.note: in absolute terms（按绝对数）vs in relative terms / in percentage terms（按相对比例）。

words.definition: The change expressed as a percentage of the starting value.

examples.en: The relative change looks big because we started from a small base.
examples.zh: 相对变化看起来很大，是因为基数很小。

words.note: 相关说法：from a low base（基数低）。

words.definition: The difference between two numbers, such as actual minus target.

examples.en: The delta between forecast and actual is about $15,000.
examples.zh: 预测与实际之间的差值约为1.5万元。

words.note: IT/金融圈常用；普通听众面前用 difference 更易懂。

words.definition: How fast something is growing, usually as a percentage per period.

examples.en: The growth rate has slowed from 8% to 5% a month.
examples.zh: 增长率从每月8%放缓到了5%。

words.definition: The relationship between two numbers, such as 3 to 1.

examples.en: The ratio of support staff to customers is about one to 500.
examples.zh: 支持人员与客户的比例大约是1比500。

words.note: 3:1 读作 three to one。

words.definition: The part of a total that belongs to one group, often as a percentage.

examples.en: Mobile's share of total traffic has grown to 58%.
examples.zh: 移动端在总流量中的占比上升到了58%。

words.note: market share = 市场份额；share of wallet = 钱包份额。

words.definition: Make up a certain part of a total.

examples.en: Enterprise clients account for 70% of revenue.
examples.zh: 企业客户占收入的70%。

words.note: account for 还有“解释（原因）”的意思：That accounts for the spike（这就解释了那个峰值）。

words.definition: Form a certain part of a total.

examples.en: Contractors make up about a fifth of the team.
examples.zh: 合同工约占团队的五分之一。

words.definition: A part of a whole, compared with the whole.

examples.en: A small proportion of users generate most of the load.
examples.zh: 一小部分用户产生了大部分负载。

words.definition: More than half of a group.

examples.en: The majority of incidents were resolved within four hours.
examples.zh: 大多数事件在四小时内得到解决。

words.note: 反义：a minority of（少数）。the vast majority = 绝大多数。

words.definition: Short forms for thousand, million and billion used on slides, as in $250k or 1.2m users.

examples.en: We're at 1.2 million users, so 1.2m on the slide.
examples.zh: 我们有120万用户，所以幻灯片上写1.2m。

words.note: 中文“万”“亿”要换算：1万 = 10 thousand（10k），10万 = 100k，100万 = 1 million，1亿 = 100 million。英语以千为单位，不按“万”。

words.definition: A digit after the decimal point; used when saying how precisely a number is shown.

examples.en: I've rounded everything to one decimal place.
examples.zh: 我把所有数字都保留到一位小数。

words.note: 4.5% 读作 four point five percent；0.5 读作 nought point five（英式）或 zero point five。

words.definition: Change a number to a simpler one that is close to it.

examples.en: Numbers may not add up to 100% due to rounding.
examples.zh: 由于四舍五入，各项相加可能不等于100%。

examples.en: I've rounded this up to $2 million.
examples.zh: 我把它向上取整为200万元。

words.note: round up 向上取整，round down 向下取整，round to the nearest thousand 四舍五入到千位。

words.definition: For each, as in cost per user or tickets per day.

examples.en: Cost per user has dropped to $14 a month.
examples.zh: 每个用户的成本降到了每月14元。

words.note: 口语里常用 a 代替 per：$14 a month、three times a week。

words.definition: Compared with; written vs on slides.

examples.en: This is actual versus budget for each department.
examples.zh: 这是各部门的实际数对比预算。

words.note: 幻灯片上写 vs 或 vs.，读出来是 versus。

words.definition: The twelve-month period a company uses for its accounts and budgets.

examples.en: We're three months into the financial year, so it's too early to call.
examples.zh: 财年才过去三个月，现在下结论还太早。

words.note: 新西兰常说 financial year（FY）；美式说 fiscal year。新西兰的税务年度是4月1日到次年3月31日，但各公司的财年不一定相同。

words.definition: The first half of a year, written H1; H2 is the second half.

examples.en: H1 revenue came in slightly ahead of plan.
examples.zh: 上半年收入略高于计划。

words.note: 读作 H-one；Q1–Q4 是第一到第四季度，读作 Q-one。要说明是自然年还是财年的 H1。

words.definition: Go up in number or level; also a noun meaning an increase.

examples.en: Costs rose steadily throughout the year.
examples.zh: 全年成本稳步上升。

examples.en: There was a sharp rise in errors on Tuesday.
examples.zh: 周二错误数量急剧上升。

words.note: rise 不及物（rise-rose-risen，后面不接宾语）；raise 及物（We raised prices 我们提高了价格）。

words.definition: Become bigger in number or amount; also a noun.

examples.en: The number of active users increased in every region.
examples.zh: 每个地区的活跃用户数都增加了。

words.note: 动词重音在后 in-CREASE，名词重音在前 IN-crease。

words.definition: Become larger over time, often used for revenue, users or a business.

examples.en: Our customer base grew by 15% last year.
examples.zh: 去年我们的客户群增长了15%。

words.note: 名词 growth：strong growth、slower growth。

words.definition: An everyday spoken phrase for increase.

examples.en: Page views went up again in October.
examples.zh: 十月浏览量又上升了。

words.definition: Rise steadily, often over a period of time.

examples.en: Cloud spend has been climbing every month since June.
examples.zh: 从六月起云支出每个月都在攀升。

words.definition: Increase suddenly by a large amount.

examples.en: Sign-ups jumped 40% the day after the email went out.
examples.zh: 邮件发出后的第二天注册量猛增了40%。

words.note: 名词也可：a big jump in sign-ups。

words.definition: Increase suddenly and strongly, often because of an event.

examples.en: Traffic surged during the Black Friday sale.
examples.zh: 黑色星期五促销期间流量激增。

words.note: 名词：a surge in demand（需求激增）。

words.definition: Rise very quickly to a high level.

examples.en: Storage costs have soared since we started keeping full logs.
examples.zh: 自从开始保留全部日志，存储成本飙升。

words.definition: A sudden, short increase that quickly goes back down; also used as a verb.

examples.en: You can see a spike in CPU usage at 2 a.m. every night.
examples.zh: 可以看到每晚凌晨两点CPU使用率都有一个尖峰。

examples.en: Errors spiked briefly after the deployment.
examples.zh: 部署后错误数短暂飙升。

words.note: spike 强调“短暂”，很快又回落；surge 可以持续一段时间。

words.definition: Rise extremely quickly; informal.

examples.en: Downloads rocketed after the app was featured in the store.
examples.zh: 应用被应用商店推荐后，下载量猛涨。

words.definition: Rise slowly by a small amount.

examples.en: The error rate edged up from 0.8% to 0.9%.
examples.zh: 错误率从0.8%小幅上升到0.9%。

words.definition: Rise slowly, often in a way people may not notice.

examples.en: Average handling time has been creeping up over the last few months.
examples.zh: 过去几个月平均处理时长一直在缓慢上升。

words.note: creep up 常带一点负面、需要警惕的意思。

words.definition: Start to increase or improve again after a slow period.

examples.en: Demand usually picks up again in February.
examples.zh: 需求通常在二月重新回升。

words.definition: Return to a normal or earlier level after a fall.

examples.en: Conversion has recovered to where it was before the outage.
examples.zh: 转化率已恢复到故障前的水平。

words.note: 名词 recovery：a full recovery、a slow recovery。

words.definition: Rise again quickly after a fall.

examples.en: Usage rebounded strongly in the second half of the month.
examples.zh: 下半月使用量强劲反弹。

words.note: 动词重音 ri-BOUND，名词 REE-bound。

words.definition: Return quickly to a previous level after a drop.

examples.en: Sales dipped in January but bounced back in February.
examples.zh: 销售额一月下滑，但二月就反弹回来了。

words.definition: Go down in number or level; also a noun.

examples.en: Response times fell after we added the cache.
examples.zh: 加了缓存后响应时间下降了。

words.note: fall-fell-fallen。注意 fall 不及物：不能说 We fell the costs，要说 We cut / reduced the costs。

words.definition: Go down, often suddenly; also a noun.

examples.en: Traffic dropped by about 20% over the long weekend.
examples.zh: 长周末期间流量下降了约20%。

words.note: drop 既可不及物（Sales dropped），也可及物（We dropped the price）。

words.definition: Go down gradually; a slightly formal word, also a noun.

examples.en: The number of on-premises servers has declined steadily.
examples.zh: 本地服务器的数量在稳步减少。

words.note: decline 还有“拒绝”的意思，汇报语境下指下降。

words.definition: Become smaller in number or amount; also a noun.

examples.en: Average cost per ticket decreased by 9%.
examples.zh: 每张工单的平均成本下降了9%。

words.note: 动词重音 dee-CREASE，名词 DEE-crease。

words.definition: An everyday spoken phrase for decrease.

examples.en: The backlog has gone down a lot since we added two people.
examples.zh: 加了两个人之后积压减少了很多。

words.definition: Fall slightly or briefly before going back up; also a noun.

examples.en: There's a small dip in December, which is normal for the holidays.
examples.zh: 十二月有一个小幅回落，节假日期间这很正常。

words.definition: Fall slightly, often from a good level.

examples.en: Customer satisfaction slipped to 86% this quarter.
examples.zh: 本季度客户满意度略降到86%。

words.note: also slip below（跌破）：slipped below the 90% target。

words.definition: Fall quickly and by a large amount.

examples.en: Open rates tumbled after we changed the email subject lines.
examples.zh: 改了邮件标题后打开率大幅下跌。

words.definition: Fall suddenly and steeply.

examples.en: Orders plunged during the outage.
examples.zh: 故障期间订单骤降。

words.definition: Fall very quickly and a very long way.

examples.en: Sign-ups plummeted when the payment page was broken.
examples.zh: 支付页面出问题时注册量直线下降。

words.note: plunge / plummet / tumble 都是“暴跌”，程度强，汇报里不要滥用。

words.definition: Fall suddenly and stay low; also a noun for a period of low activity.

examples.en: Sales slumped in the winter months.
examples.zh: 冬季几个月销售持续低迷。

words.definition: Fall slowly by a small amount.

examples.en: Unit costs edged down again this month.
examples.zh: 单位成本本月又小幅下降。

words.note: 也说 edge lower / tick down。

words.definition: Gradually become smaller until it almost stops.

examples.en: The spike in calls tapered off by the end of the week.
examples.zh: 来电高峰到周末逐渐减弱了。

words.definition: Stay at about the same level with no real increase or decrease.

examples.en: Revenue remained flat quarter-on-quarter.
examples.zh: 收入季度环比持平。

words.note: 也说 stay flat、be flat；flat 在这里是“没变化”，不是“扁平”。

words.definition: Stay at a steady level without big changes.

examples.en: The error rate has remained stable at around 0.5%.
examples.zh: 错误率一直稳定在0.5%左右。

words.note: 也说 remain steady、hold steady。

words.definition: Stop rising or falling and stay at a steady level.

examples.en: Growth has started to level off after a strong first quarter.
examples.zh: 第一季度强劲增长后，增长开始趋于平稳。

words.note: 也说 level out、flatten out。

words.definition: A period where the value stops growing and stays level; also a verb.

examples.en: User numbers have plateaued at around 50,000.
examples.zh: 用户数量停滞在5万左右。

examples.en: We've hit a plateau, so we need a new channel to keep growing.
examples.zh: 我们进入了平台期，需要新的渠道才能继续增长。

words.note: 新西兰/英式重音在前：PLAT-oh；美式重音在后：pla-TOH。复数 plateaus 或 plateaux。

words.definition: Stop growing or developing, in a way that is a problem.

examples.en: Organic traffic has stagnated for most of the year.
examples.zh: 自然流量今年大部分时间都停滞不前。

words.note: 比 level off 更负面；名词 stagnation。

words.definition: Go up and down irregularly.

examples.en: Daily orders fluctuate a lot, so I'm showing a weekly average.
examples.zh: 每日订单波动很大，所以我展示的是周平均值。

words.note: 名词 fluctuation；fluctuate between X and Y = 在X和Y之间波动。

words.definition: Stay close to a certain level, moving only slightly above and below it.

examples.en: Uptime has hovered around 99.95% all year.
examples.zh: 全年正常运行时间都在99.95%左右徘徊。

words.definition: Reach the highest point; also a noun for that point.

examples.en: Traffic peaked at 12,000 concurrent users on launch day.
examples.zh: 上线当天流量达到峰值，有1.2万并发用户。

examples.en: The peak was in mid-December.
examples.zh: 峰值出现在十二月中旬。

words.note: peak 是动词也是名词；peak hours = 高峰时段。

words.definition: Reach the highest level ever recorded.

examples.en: Monthly revenue hit a record high in November.
examples.zh: 十一月月收入创历史新高。

words.note: hit a high / hit a low = 达到高点/低点；hit an all-time low = 创历史新低。

words.definition: Reach the lowest point and stop falling.

examples.en: We think the decline has bottomed out and we're starting to see a recovery.
examples.zh: 我们认为下滑已经触底，开始看到复苏迹象。

words.definition: The lowest point between two higher points on a chart.

examples.en: The trough in July lines up with the school holidays.
examples.zh: 七月的低谷与学校假期时间吻合。

words.note: peak（峰）和 trough（谷）是一对。peaks and troughs = 起起落落。

words.definition: Get to a certain level.

examples.en: We expect to reach 100,000 users by the end of the year.
examples.zh: 我们预计年底达到10万用户。

words.note: reach 后面直接接数值，不加 to：reach 10%（不说 reach to 10%）。

words.definition: Be at a certain level at a given time.

examples.en: As at the end of June, the backlog stood at 340 tickets.
examples.zh: 截至六月底，积压工单为340张。

words.note: 描述某一时刻的数值很常用：The figure currently stands at…

words.definition: Do better than another group, a target or a benchmark.

examples.en: The new onboarding flow outperformed the old one on every metric.
examples.zh: 新的入门流程在每个指标上都优于旧流程。

words.definition: Do worse than expected or worse than a comparison group.

examples.en: The Wellington store has underperformed for three months in a row.
examples.zh: 惠灵顿门店已经连续三个月表现不及预期。

words.definition: Become larger or higher than something that was ahead before.

examples.en: Mobile overtook desktop as our main channel in March.
examples.zh: 三月份移动端超过桌面端，成为我们的主要渠道。

words.note: 也可以说 surpass（较正式）。

words.definition: A general pattern of values increasing over time.

examples.en: Despite the dip in May, the overall upward trend continues.
examples.zh: 尽管五月有所回落，整体上升趋势仍在持续。

words.note: 也说 an upward trajectory；动词说法：trend upward(s)。

words.definition: A general pattern of values decreasing over time.

examples.en: Call volumes have been on a downward trend since we launched chat.
examples.zh: 自上线在线聊天以来，来电量一直呈下降趋势。

words.definition: Move generally higher over a period, even with ups and downs.

examples.en: Costs are trending upward, so we need to keep an eye on them.
examples.zh: 成本呈上升趋势，我们需要持续关注。

words.note: 美式多用 upward，英式也常说 upwards。也说 trend higher / trend lower。

words.definition: The moment when a trend changes direction.

examples.en: The new pricing in April was a clear turning point.
examples.zh: 四月推出的新定价是一个明显的转折点。

words.note: 数学/统计上的“拐点”是 inflection point，商务口语里也常用来指“拐点”。

words.definition: A point where the shape or direction of a trend changes significantly.

examples.en: We may be at an inflection point: growth is slowing after two strong years.
examples.zh: 我们可能正处在拐点：经过两年强劲增长后增速在放缓。

words.definition: Change to the opposite direction.

examples.en: The new feature helped reverse the decline in engagement.
examples.zh: 新功能帮助扭转了活跃度下降的局面。

words.note: 名词：a reversal（逆转），a trend reversal。

words.definition: Happen or grow faster.

examples.en: Growth accelerated in the second half of the year.
examples.zh: 下半年增长加速了。

words.definition: Happen or grow more slowly.

examples.en: Growth has slowed down, but it's still positive.
examples.zh: 增长放缓了，但仍然是正增长。

words.note: growth slowed 增速放缓 ≠ 下降，数值仍在增长。注意区分 slowing growth 和 decline。

words.definition: Start to grow or progress faster and more strongly.

examples.en: Adoption of the new tool is really gaining momentum.
examples.zh: 新工具的采用率势头越来越强。

words.note: 反义：lose momentum（势头减弱）。

words.definition: Grow or move faster than something else.

examples.en: Costs are outpacing revenue, which is squeezing our margin.
examples.zh: 成本增速超过收入，正在挤压我们的利润率。

words.definition: Be slower or lower than something else.

examples.en: The South Island lags behind the North Island on adoption.
examples.zh: 南岛的采用率落后于北岛。

words.note: lag 还指“滞后”：there's a lag of two weeks（有两周滞后）。

words.definition: Become larger, used for a gap or difference.

examples.en: The gap between forecast and actual widened in the last quarter.
examples.zh: 最后一个季度预测与实际的差距扩大了。

words.definition: Become smaller, used for a gap or difference.

examples.en: The gap between the two teams has narrowed to just two points.
examples.zh: 两个团队之间的差距缩小到只有两个百分点。

words.note: close the gap = 消除差距。

words.definition: Become steady after a period of change.

examples.en: After the fix, memory usage stabilised at around 60%.
examples.zh: 修复后内存使用率稳定在60%左右。

words.note: 美式拼写 stabilize；名词 stabilisation。

words.definition: Small in size or amount.

examples.en: There was a slight increase in the error rate.
examples.zh: 错误率略有上升。

examples.en: Costs rose slightly in Q3.
examples.zh: 第三季度成本略有上升。

words.note: 形容词 slight + 名词（a slight drop）；副词 slightly + 动词（dropped slightly）。

words.definition: Very small and not very important.

examples.en: The difference between the two options is marginal.
examples.zh: 两个方案的差别很小。

examples.en: Revenue was marginally higher than last month.
examples.zh: 收入比上个月略高一点。

words.note: marginal cost 在经济学里是“边际成本”。

words.definition: Fairly small, but usually positive.

examples.en: We saw a modest improvement in retention.
examples.zh: 留存率有小幅改善。

words.note: modest 带一点“虽然不大，但还不错”的语气。

words.definition: Neither very small nor very large.

examples.en: We expect moderate growth next year, around 5%.
examples.zh: 我们预计明年增长适中，约为5%。

words.definition: Changing at a regular, even rate, without big jumps.

examples.en: There's been a steady increase in mobile usage.
examples.zh: 移动端使用量稳步增长。

examples.en: Revenue has grown steadily over the past two years.
examples.zh: 过去两年收入稳步增长。

words.note: steady increase = 稳步增长（速度均匀）；stable = 保持不变。

words.definition: Happening slowly over a long period.

examples.en: We've seen a gradual decline in desktop traffic.
examples.zh: 桌面端流量在逐渐下降。

examples.en: Adoption has gradually picked up.
examples.zh: 采用率逐渐回升。

words.definition: Staying the same or following the same pattern over time.

examples.en: We've had consistent growth of 2 to 3% every month.
examples.zh: 我们每月都保持着2%到3%的稳定增长。

words.note: consistently above target = 一直高于目标。

words.definition: Large or important enough to notice; in statistics it has a stricter meaning.

examples.en: There's been a significant drop in support calls.
examples.zh: 支持来电显著减少。

words.note: 在数据会议里要小心：significant 可能被理解为“统计显著”。如果没做检验，可以说 a large / notable drop。

words.definition: Large in amount or importance.

examples.en: The new storage tier gives us substantial savings.
examples.zh: 新的存储层级为我们节省了可观的费用。

words.definition: Fairly large; a formal word.

examples.en: This would require considerable effort from the data team.
examples.zh: 这需要数据团队投入相当大的精力。

words.definition: Sudden and large.

examples.en: There's a sharp drop in traffic right after the outage.
examples.zh: 故障之后流量急剧下降。

examples.en: Costs rose sharply in August.
examples.zh: 八月成本急剧上升。

words.definition: Very large and sudden.

examples.en: We've seen a dramatic improvement in page load times.
examples.zh: 页面加载时间有了巨大改善。

examples.en: Usage fell dramatically when the free tier ended.
examples.zh: 免费版结束后使用量大幅下降。

words.note: 比 sharp 更强，汇报时注意不要夸大。

words.definition: Rising or falling at a sharp angle on a chart.

examples.en: The steep rise in March is the new client coming on board.
examples.zh: 三月的陡峭上升是因为新客户签约入驻。

words.note: a steep learning curve = 学习难度大。

words.definition: Happening very quickly.

examples.en: The rapid growth in data volume is pushing up our storage bill.
examples.zh: 数据量的快速增长正在推高存储费用。

examples.en: Costs are rising rapidly.
examples.zh: 成本在快速上升。

words.definition: Happening quickly and unexpectedly.

examples.en: Can anyone explain the sudden spike on the 14th?
examples.zh: 有人能解释一下14号的突然飙升吗？

words.definition: Big enough to be seen or noticed.

examples.en: There's a noticeable difference in conversion between the two pages.
examples.zh: 两个页面的转化率有明显差异。

words.definition: Clear and easy to notice; a slightly formal word.

examples.en: There's been a marked improvement since the new process started.
examples.zh: 新流程启用以来有了明显改善。

words.note: markedly（副词，读 MAR-kid-lee）= 明显地。

words.definition: So small that it is not important.

examples.en: The impact on performance is negligible, less than one millisecond.
examples.zh: 对性能的影响可以忽略不计，不到一毫秒。

words.definition: Changing a lot, often quickly and unpredictably.

examples.en: Weekly numbers are quite volatile, so focus on the monthly trend.
examples.zh: 每周数据波动很大，所以请关注月度趋势。

words.note: 名词 volatility（波动性）。美式读 VOL-uh-tul。

words.definition: Continuing for a long time.

examples.en: We've had sustained growth for six quarters in a row.
examples.zh: 我们已连续六个季度持续增长。

words.definition: Large and positive, used for growth, demand or performance.

examples.en: We had a strong quarter, with revenue up 11%.
examples.zh: 我们这个季度表现强劲，收入增长了11%。

words.note: strong growth / strong demand；反义 weak 或较委婉的 soft。

words.definition: Weaker than expected; a polite way to describe disappointing numbers.

examples.en: Demand was a bit soft in the first two weeks of the month.
examples.zh: 本月前两周需求有点疲软。

words.note: soft、softer、softening 是委婉说法，比 weak / bad 更常用于汇报。

words.definition: At a good, positive level.

examples.en: We're seeing healthy growth in the SME segment.
examples.zh: 中小企业板块增长良好。

words.definition: Not going up or down.

examples.en: Headcount was flat year-on-year.
examples.zh: 人数同比持平。

words.note: flat 在这里是“没变化”；a flat fee 是“固定费用”。

words.definition: Small and not very important.

examples.en: There were a few minor fluctuations, but nothing unusual.
examples.zh: 有一些小波动，但没有异常。

words.definition: Very sudden and unexpected, often in a negative way.

examples.en: There's an abrupt drop on the 3rd, which turned out to be a tracking issue.
examples.zh: 3号有一个骤降，后来发现是埋点问题。

words.definition: Never having happened before.

examples.en: We had an unprecedented number of sign-ups on launch day.
examples.zh: 上线当天注册量前所未有。

words.note: 分量很重，只在真正的历史新高时使用。

words.definition: Changing often and without any clear pattern.

examples.en: The data from that sensor is erratic, so I've excluded it.
examples.zh: 那个传感器的数据忽高忽低，所以我把它排除了。

words.definition: Strong and healthy; for analysis, reliable and not easily affected by errors.

examples.en: Growth remains robust across all regions.
examples.zh: 所有地区的增长依然强劲。

examples.en: The result is robust: it holds even when we remove the outliers.
examples.zh: 这个结果很稳健：去掉异常值后依然成立。

words.definition: Increasing in small steps; also the extra amount added by a change.

examples.en: The campaign brought in about $40,000 of incremental revenue.
examples.zh: 这次活动带来了约4万元的增量收入。

words.definition: The typical value of a group of numbers; in everyday talk, usually the mean.

examples.en: On average, each customer raises two tickets a month.
examples.zh: 平均每个客户每月提交两张工单。

words.note: on average = 平均来说；口语的 average 一般指 mean（算术平均），但最好说清楚是 mean 还是 median。

words.definition: The total of all values divided by how many values there are.

examples.en: The mean response time is 2.4 seconds, but a few very slow requests pull it up.
examples.zh: 平均响应时间是2.4秒，但少数特别慢的请求把它拉高了。

words.note: mean 受极端值影响大；有长尾时用 median 更能代表“典型值”。

words.definition: The middle value when all the values are sorted from smallest to largest.

examples.en: The median deal size is $8,000, so half our deals are smaller than that.
examples.zh: 成交额中位数是8000元，所以一半的单子比这个小。

words.definition: The value that appears most often in a set of data.

examples.en: The mode is five stars, but the average is pulled down by a few one-star reviews.
examples.zh: 众数是五星，但几条一星评价把平均分拉低了。

words.definition: The spread between the lowest and highest values.

examples.en: Resolution times range from ten minutes to three days.
examples.zh: 解决时间从十分钟到三天不等。

words.note: range from X to Y = 从X到Y不等；统计上 range = 最大值减最小值（极差）。

words.definition: How the values in a dataset are spread out across the possible range.

examples.en: This histogram shows the distribution of order values.
examples.zh: 这张直方图展示了订单金额的分布。

words.definition: A symmetrical, bell-shaped distribution where most values are near the average.

examples.en: Session lengths don't follow a normal distribution; there's a long tail on the right.
examples.zh: 会话时长不服从正态分布；右侧有一条长尾。

words.note: 也叫 bell curve（钟形曲线）。

words.definition: Not symmetrical, with more values bunched on one side and a long tail on the other.

examples.en: The data is right-skewed, so the mean is higher than the median.
examples.zh: 数据右偏，所以平均数高于中位数。

words.note: right-skewed / positively skewed = 右偏（长尾在右）。skewed by 还可表示“被……扭曲”：skewed by one big order。

words.definition: A small number of very large values stretching far out from the rest of the distribution.

examples.en: There's a long tail of very slow requests that we need to look at.
examples.zh: 有一条由非常慢的请求组成的长尾，我们需要研究一下。

words.definition: A value that is much higher or lower than the rest of the data.

examples.en: I've removed one outlier: a test account with 50,000 logins.
examples.zh: 我去掉了一个异常值：一个有5万次登录的测试账号。

words.definition: A measure of how far values are spread from the mean; in finance it also means the gap between actual and budget.

examples.en: There's a lot of variance between teams, so the overall average hides a lot.
examples.zh: 团队之间差异很大，所以总体平均值掩盖了很多信息。

words.note: 统计里 variance = 方差；财务汇报里 variance = 差异（实际与预算之差），见 budget variance。

words.definition: A measure of how spread out values are around the mean; a small one means values are close together.

examples.en: The standard deviation is small, so most days are close to the average.
examples.zh: 标准差很小，所以大部分日子都接近平均值。

words.note: 缩写 SD 或 std dev，希腊字母 σ（sigma）。

words.definition: The value below which a given percentage of the data falls.

examples.en: The 95th percentile response time is 800 milliseconds.
examples.zh: 响应时间的第95百分位数是800毫秒。

examples.en: Our P99 latency spiked during the release.
examples.zh: 发布期间我们的P99延迟飙升。

words.note: P95 读作 P ninety-five，意思是95%的请求不超过这个值。IT 监控里很常用。

words.definition: One of three values that split sorted data into four equal parts.

examples.en: Teams in the top quartile close tickets twice as fast.
examples.zh: 排在前四分之一的团队关闭工单的速度快一倍。

words.note: top quartile = 前25%；bottom quartile = 后25%。

words.definition: The spread of the middle 50% of the data, from the first to the third quartile.

examples.en: The interquartile range is fairly narrow, so most deals are a similar size.
examples.zh: 四分位距比较窄，说明大部分单子规模相近。

words.note: 缩写 IQR；箱线图里箱子的长度就是 IQR。

words.definition: A smaller group taken from a larger population and used to draw conclusions about it.

examples.en: We surveyed a random sample of 400 customers.
examples.zh: 我们随机抽取了400名客户进行调查。

words.definition: The number of people or items in a sample.

examples.en: The sample size is only 30, so I wouldn't read too much into it.
examples.zh: 样本量只有30，所以我不会过度解读。

words.note: 缩写 n：n = 30。

words.definition: In statistics, the whole group you want to know about, not just the sample.

examples.en: The population here is all active customers, about 12,000 accounts.
examples.zh: 这里的总体是所有活跃客户，约1.2万个账户。

words.note: 统计里 population 不一定是“人口”，指被研究的全部对象。

words.definition: How much a survey result might differ from the true value, shown as plus or minus.

examples.en: Satisfaction is 78%, with a margin of error of plus or minus four points.
examples.zh: 满意度为78%，误差范围为正负4个百分点。

words.note: ± 读作 plus or minus。

words.definition: A range of values that is likely to contain the true value, at a stated level of confidence.

examples.en: The 95% confidence interval for the uplift is between 2% and 6%.
examples.zh: 提升幅度的95%置信区间在2%到6%之间。

words.note: 缩写 CI；confidence level（置信水平）是 95% 那个数。

words.definition: Unlikely to be caused by chance alone, based on a statistical test.

examples.en: The difference between version A and version B is statistically significant.
examples.zh: A版本和B版本之间的差异在统计上显著。

words.note: 和日常的 significant（很大）不同：差异可以很小但统计显著，也可以看起来很大却不显著。

words.definition: The probability of seeing a result at least this extreme if there were really no effect; smaller means stronger evidence.

examples.en: The p-value is 0.02, which is below our 0.05 threshold.
examples.zh: P值是0.02，低于我们0.05的阈值。

words.definition: A relationship where two measures tend to move together.

examples.en: There's a strong correlation between training completion and fewer incidents.
examples.zh: 完成培训与事件减少之间有很强的相关性。

words.definition: When one thing actually makes another thing happen.

examples.en: This shows correlation, not causation: both could be driven by company size.
examples.zh: 这显示的是相关性而不是因果关系：两者可能都受公司规模影响。

words.definition: A relationship where one value tends to go up when the other goes up.

examples.en: There's a positive correlation between team size and ticket volume.
examples.zh: 团队规模与工单量呈正相关。

words.definition: A relationship where one value tends to go down when the other goes up.

examples.en: We see a negative correlation between page load time and conversion.
examples.zh: 页面加载时间与转化率呈负相关。

words.note: 也叫 inverse correlation。

words.definition: A number from minus one to plus one showing how strongly two measures move together.

examples.en: The correlation coefficient is 0.8, which is a strong relationship.
examples.zh: 相关系数是0.8，相关性很强。

words.note: 常用字母 r 表示：r = 0.8。

words.definition: A statistical method for estimating how one value changes with one or more other values.

examples.en: We ran a regression to estimate the effect of price on demand.
examples.zh: 我们做了回归分析来估计价格对需求的影响。

words.note: linear regression = 线性回归。日常 regression 也指软件的“回归缺陷”，要看语境。

words.definition: A number from 0 to 1 showing how much of the variation a model explains.

examples.en: The R-squared is 0.65, so the model explains about two-thirds of the variation.
examples.zh: R方是0.65，模型解释了约三分之二的变化。

words.note: 也写作 R²。

words.definition: The starting level or normal level that you compare new results against.

examples.en: Compared with the baseline, the new process cut processing time by 30%.
examples.zh: 与基线相比，新流程把处理时间缩短了30%。

words.note: baseline period = 基准期。在图表上也指作为参照的那条线。

words.definition: The group in a test that does not get the change, used for comparison.

examples.en: The control group kept the old checkout page.
examples.zh: 对照组保留了旧的结账页面。

words.note: 接受改动的那组叫 test group / treatment group（实验组）。

words.definition: An experiment that shows two versions to similar groups to see which performs better.

examples.en: We ran an A/B test on the sign-up button for two weeks.
examples.zh: 我们对注册按钮做了两周的A/B测试。

words.note: 读作 A-B test；也说 split test。

words.definition: A regular pattern that repeats at certain times of the year, month or week.

examples.en: There's strong seasonality: December is always our busiest month.
examples.zh: 季节性很明显：十二月总是我们最忙的月份。

words.definition: Changed to remove regular seasonal patterns so the underlying trend is clearer.

examples.en: On a seasonally adjusted basis, demand was actually up slightly.
examples.zh: 经季节性调整后，需求实际上略有上升。

words.definition: An average that is recalculated over a sliding window, such as the last seven days, to smooth out noise.

examples.en: The thick line is the seven-day moving average.
examples.zh: 那条粗线是七日移动平均线。

words.note: 也说 rolling average（滚动平均），意思相同；7-day rolling average 很常见。

words.definition: An average where some values count more than others, for example by size.

examples.en: I've used a weighted average, so bigger customers count for more.
examples.zh: 我用了加权平均，所以大客户的权重更高。

words.definition: Adding up over time, so each value includes everything before it.

examples.en: This line shows cumulative sign-ups since launch.
examples.zh: 这条线显示了自上线以来的累计注册量。

words.note: cumulative total = 累计总数；running total 意思相同。

words.definition: A set of data points recorded at regular time intervals.

examples.en: We have a clean time series going back to 2021.
examples.zh: 我们有一份从2021年开始的完整时间序列数据。

words.note: series 单复数同形。

words.definition: Estimate future or unknown values by extending a current trend.

examples.en: If we extrapolate the current trend, we'll hit capacity by March.
examples.zh: 如果按当前趋势外推，我们将在三月达到容量上限。

words.note: 外推有风险，讲的时候常加 if the trend continues。

words.definition: Estimate a missing value between two known values.

examples.en: Two days of data were missing, so I interpolated them.
examples.zh: 有两天的数据缺失，所以我做了插值。

words.definition: Random variation in data that does not reflect a real change.

examples.en: A lot of the day-to-day movement is just noise.
examples.zh: 很多每天的波动只是噪声。

words.note: signal vs noise：真实信号与随机噪声。

words.definition: A real pattern or change in the data, as opposed to random noise.

examples.en: The question is whether this drop is a real signal or just noise.
examples.zh: 问题是这次下降是真实信号还是只是噪声。

words.definition: When a sample does not fairly represent the population, so results are distorted.

examples.en: Only happy customers answer the survey, so there's some sampling bias.
examples.zh: 只有满意的客户回复了调查，所以存在一定的抽样偏差。

words.note: 相关：survivorship bias（幸存者偏差），selection bias（选择偏差）。

words.definition: A third factor that affects both things you are comparing and can create a false relationship.

examples.en: Company size is a confounding factor here: bigger companies use more features and also renew more.
examples.zh: 公司规模在这里是一个混杂因素：大公司使用更多功能，续约率也更高。

words.note: 也说 confounding variable、confounder。

words.definition: An idea you want to test with data.

examples.en: Our hypothesis is that faster onboarding leads to higher retention.
examples.zh: 我们的假设是更快的上手流程会带来更高的留存率。

words.note: 复数 hypotheses（读 hy-POTH-uh-seez）。assumption 是“前提假设”，hypothesis 是“待检验的假设”。

words.definition: A group of users who share a starting point, such as everyone who signed up in January.

examples.en: The January cohort has the best twelve-month retention.
examples.zh: 一月份注册的同期群十二个月留存率最好。

words.note: cohort analysis = 同期群分析。

words.definition: How often something happens, or how many times each value appears.

examples.en: The frequency of outages has dropped from monthly to once a quarter.
examples.zh: 故障频率从每月一次下降到每季度一次。

words.definition: An estimate of a future value based on current data and trends.

examples.en: Based on current growth, our projection is 15,000 users by June.
examples.zh: 按目前的增长，我们预测到六月有1.5万用户。

words.note: projection 多基于趋势外推；forecast 更正式，指正式的预测数。

words.definition: A careful guess at a number based on the information available.

examples.en: This is an estimate, because we only have three weeks of data.
examples.zh: 这是估算值，因为我们只有三周的数据。

words.note: 名词读 ES-tih-mut，动词读 ES-tih-mate。

words.definition: Key performance indicator: one of the most important numbers used to judge how well something is going.

examples.en: Our three KPIs this year are uptime, customer satisfaction and cost per user.
examples.zh: 今年我们的三个KPI是正常运行时间、客户满意度和每用户成本。

words.definition: A number used to measure something, such as page views or response time.

examples.en: This metric is easy to measure but doesn't tell us much about value.
examples.zh: 这个指标容易测量，但不太能说明价值。

words.note: 所有 KPI 都是 metric，但不是所有 metric 都是 KPI。vanity metric = 好看但没意义的指标。

words.definition: The number you are aiming to reach.

examples.en: We're at 92% against a target of 95%.
examples.zh: 我们目前是92%，目标是95%。

examples.en: We hit our target two weeks early.
examples.zh: 我们提前两周达到了目标。

words.note: 常用搭配：hit / meet target（达标），miss target（未达标），ahead of / behind target（超前/落后于目标）。

words.definition: A standard or reference point, often from other companies, used for comparison.

examples.en: Our churn is well below the industry benchmark.
examples.zh: 我们的流失率远低于行业基准。

words.note: 也可作动词：We benchmarked our costs against similar companies。

words.definition: The real figures that happened, as opposed to the budget or forecast.

examples.en: These are actuals up to the end of September and forecast after that.
examples.zh: 九月底之前是实际数，之后是预测数。

words.note: 财务汇报里常用复数 actuals；actual vs budget（实际对比预算）简称 AvB。

words.definition: The planned amount of money for a period.

examples.en: We're about $20,000 under budget for the year.
examples.zh: 我们今年比预算少花了约2万元。

words.note: under budget = 低于预算（省钱）；over budget = 超预算；on budget = 符合预算。

words.definition: The difference between the actual figure and the budget.

examples.en: The biggest budget variance is in contractor costs.
examples.zh: 最大的预算差异在合同工成本上。

words.note: favourable variance = 有利差异（比预算好）；unfavourable / adverse variance = 不利差异。

words.definition: An official estimate of future figures, usually updated during the year.

examples.en: We've revised the full-year forecast down by 3%.
examples.zh: 我们把全年预测下调了3%。

words.note: 过去式 forecast 或 forecasted 都可以。revise up / down = 上调/下调。

words.definition: Money a business receives from selling its products or services.

examples.en: Subscription revenue grew 14% year-on-year.
examples.zh: 订阅收入同比增长14%。

words.note: revenue 是收入（销售额），profit 是利润，两个不要混。

words.definition: What is left from revenue after costs are taken away.

examples.en: Profit was down even though revenue was up, because costs grew faster.
examples.zh: 尽管收入上升，利润却下降了，因为成本增长更快。

words.note: gross profit 毛利，net profit 净利润。

words.definition: Profit as a percentage of revenue.

examples.en: Our margin on hardware is much thinner than on services.
examples.zh: 我们硬件的利润率比服务薄得多。

words.note: thin / tight margin = 利润率低；margin squeeze = 利润率被挤压。

words.definition: Revenue minus the direct cost of what you sold, as a percentage of revenue.

examples.en: Gross margin improved from 38% to 41%, up three percentage points.
examples.zh: 毛利率从38%提高到41%，上升了三个百分点。

words.definition: The money spent to produce or run something.

examples.en: Cloud costs are now our second biggest line item.
examples.zh: 云成本现在是我们第二大的支出项目。

words.note: line item = 报表上的单独一行（一个科目）。

words.definition: Operating expenditure: day-to-day running costs such as salaries and subscriptions.

examples.en: Moving to the cloud shifts spend from capex to opex.
examples.zh: 迁移上云会把支出从资本支出转为运营支出。

words.note: capex（KAP-ex）= capital expenditure 资本支出，如购买服务器。

words.definition: Return on investment: how much you gain compared with what you spent.

examples.en: The automation project paid for itself in eight months, so the ROI is strong.
examples.zh: 自动化项目八个月就收回了成本，投资回报率很高。

words.note: 逐个字母读 R-O-I；payback period = 回本期。

words.definition: The percentage of people who complete a desired action, such as buying after visiting.

examples.en: The conversion rate on the new landing page is 3.2%, up from 2.5%.
examples.zh: 新落地页的转化率是3.2%，之前是2.5%。

words.definition: The percentage of customers who stop using or paying for a service in a period.

examples.en: Monthly churn rate has dropped to 1.8%.
examples.zh: 月流失率降到了1.8%。

words.note: churn 也可作动词：customers who churned（流失的客户）。

words.definition: The percentage of customers or users who keep using a product over a period.

examples.en: Thirty-day retention is 45%, which is in line with similar apps.
examples.zh: 30天留存率为45%，与同类应用持平。

words.note: retention 和 churn 大致互补：留存率90% ≈ 流失率10%。

words.definition: People who used a product in a given period, such as daily (DAU) or monthly (MAU).

examples.en: Monthly active users passed 50,000 for the first time.
examples.zh: 月活跃用户首次突破5万。

examples.en: DAU over MAU is about 20%, so people use it about six days a month.
examples.zh: 日活/月活约为20%，即用户每月大约使用六天。

words.note: DAU = daily active users（日活），MAU = monthly active users（月活）。一定要说明 active 的定义（登录？操作？）。

words.definition: Total revenue divided by the number of orders.

examples.en: Average order value rose to $86 after we added bundles.
examples.zh: 加入组合套餐后，平均订单金额升至86元。

words.note: 缩写 AOV。

words.definition: The average amount spent on sales and marketing to win one new customer.

examples.en: Customer acquisition cost has gone up because ads are more expensive.
examples.zh: 由于广告更贵，获客成本上升了。

words.note: 缩写 CAC（读 KAK 或 C-A-C）。

words.definition: The total revenue you expect from a customer over the whole relationship.

examples.en: Lifetime value is about four times acquisition cost, which is healthy.
examples.zh: 客户生命周期价值约为获客成本的四倍，这是健康的。

words.note: 缩写 LTV 或 CLV（customer lifetime value）。

words.definition: Annual recurring revenue: the yearly value of subscription contracts.

examples.en: ARR crossed $5 million this quarter.
examples.zh: 本季度年度经常性收入突破500万元。

words.note: MRR = monthly recurring revenue（月度经常性收入）。SaaS 公司常用。

words.definition: A forecast made by assuming current performance continues, often annualised.

examples.en: At the current run rate, we'll spend about $1.2 million on cloud this year.
examples.zh: 按当前水平推算，我们今年在云上大约花费120万元。

words.note: annualised run rate = 年化值（如本月×12）。注意季节性会让 run rate 失真。

words.definition: How much of the available capacity, time or resources is actually being used.

examples.en: Consultant utilisation was 78% against a target of 80%.
examples.zh: 顾问利用率为78%，目标是80%。

examples.en: CPU utilisation peaks at about 70%.
examples.zh: CPU利用率峰值约为70%。

words.note: 美式拼写 utilization。

words.definition: How much work a system or team completes in a period.

examples.en: Throughput doubled after we parallelised the jobs.
examples.zh: 把任务并行化后吞吐量翻了一倍。

words.definition: The time from a request being made to it being delivered.

examples.en: Average lead time for a new laptop is down to three days.
examples.zh: 新笔记本电脑的平均交付周期缩短到三天。

words.note: lead 读 LEED（不是“铅” LED）。cycle time 指开始做到做完的时间。

words.definition: Service level agreement: a promised level of service, such as responding within four hours.

examples.en: We met the SLA on 97% of priority-one tickets.
examples.zh: 97%的一级工单达到了服务等级协议要求。

words.note: 逐个字母读 S-L-A；breach the SLA = 违反SLA。

words.definition: The percentage of time a system is available and working.

examples.en: Uptime was 99.97% this month, above our 99.9% target.
examples.zh: 本月可用率为99.97%，高于99.9%的目标。

words.note: 99.9% 读作 ninety-nine point nine percent，俗称 three nines。反义 downtime（停机时间）。

words.definition: Mean time to resolve or repair: the average time it takes to fix an incident.

examples.en: MTTR for major incidents is down from six hours to just under four.
examples.zh: 重大事件的平均修复时间从六小时降到不到四小时。

words.note: 逐个字母读 M-T-T-R；R 可指 resolve / repair / recover，汇报时要说明定义。

words.definition: Net Promoter Score: the percentage of promoters minus the percentage of detractors, from minus 100 to plus 100.

examples.en: Our NPS went from 32 to 41 this year.
examples.zh: 我们的净推荐值今年从32升到了41。

words.note: NPS 是分数不是百分比：说 up nine points，不说 up 9%。

words.definition: How happy customers are, often measured by a short survey score.

examples.en: Customer satisfaction is steady at 4.5 out of 5.
examples.zh: 客户满意度稳定在4.5分（满分5分）。

words.note: 缩写 CSAT（读 SEE-sat）。

words.definition: The number of people employed in a team or company.

examples.en: Headcount is flat, but output is up 20%.
examples.zh: 人数持平，但产出增加了20%。

words.definition: A summary report showing several key metrics, usually against targets.

examples.en: The monthly scorecard shows five of our seven KPIs on target.
examples.zh: 月度计分卡显示七个KPI中有五个达标。

words.note: balanced scorecard = 平衡计分卡。

words.definition: Objectives and key results: a goal-setting method with an objective and a few measurable results.

examples.en: This metric is one of the key results for our Q3 OKRs.
examples.zh: 这个指标是我们第三季度OKR中的一个关键结果。

words.note: 逐个字母读 O-K-R。

words.definition: A simple traffic-light rating: red for at risk, amber for some concern, green for on track.

examples.en: Two projects are green, one is amber and one has gone red.
examples.zh: 两个项目是绿色，一个是黄色，一个变成了红色。

words.note: RAG = red, amber, green；英式/新西兰用 amber，美式常说 yellow。读作 RAG（一个词）。

words.definition: Progressing as planned and likely to hit the target.

examples.en: We're on track to meet the annual savings target.
examples.zh: 我们正按计划完成年度节省目标。

words.note: 反义：off track、behind；at risk = 有风险。

words.definition: Better than the planned figure at this point in time.

examples.en: We're slightly ahead of plan on new customers.
examples.zh: 新客户数稍微超前于计划。

words.note: behind plan = 落后于计划；in line with plan = 符合计划。

words.definition: The percentage of people who click a link after seeing it.

examples.en: The click-through rate on the newsletter was 4.1%.
examples.zh: 简报的点击率为4.1%。

words.note: 缩写 CTR。

words.definition: The number of support requests received in a period.

examples.en: Ticket volume usually spikes on the first Monday after a release.
examples.zh: 发布后的第一个周一工单量通常会飙升。

words.definition: Work that has been requested but not yet done.

examples.en: The backlog has grown to 400 items, so we need to prioritise.
examples.zh: 积压已增至400项，所以我们需要排优先级。

words.definition: The cost of producing or serving one unit, such as one user or one transaction.

examples.en: Unit cost per transaction fell from 12 cents to 9 cents.
examples.zh: 每笔交易的单位成本从12分降到9分。

words.definition: A collection of related data, usually in a table or file.

examples.en: This dataset covers all orders from January to June.
examples.zh: 这个数据集涵盖一月到六月的所有订单。

words.note: 也可写成 data set。data 可当单数（the data shows）或复数（the data show），新西兰职场多用单数。

words.definition: Where the data comes from, such as a database, system or survey.

examples.en: The data source for this chart is our CRM, as at 30 June.
examples.zh: 这张图的数据来源是我们的CRM，截至6月30日。

words.definition: Data as it was collected, before any cleaning or processing.

examples.en: I'm happy to share the raw data if anyone wants to dig into it.
examples.zh: 如果有人想深入研究，我很乐意分享原始数据。

words.definition: Fixing or removing incorrect, incomplete or duplicate data before analysis.

examples.en: Most of the time on this project went into data cleaning.
examples.zh: 这个项目大部分时间都花在了数据清洗上。

words.note: 也说 data cleansing；动词 clean the data。

words.definition: As a noun, data that is accurate and consistent; as a verb phrase, to fix messy data.

examples.en: Once we had clean data, the pattern was obvious.
examples.zh: 一旦数据清洗干净，规律就很明显了。

words.definition: Empty fields where data should be.

examples.en: About 5% of records have missing values for region.
examples.zh: 约5%的记录缺少地区字段的值。

words.note: 数据库里空值常叫 null（读 NULL）或 blank。

words.definition: Records that appear more than once in a dataset.

examples.en: We found about 300 duplicates caused by the import running twice.
examples.zh: 我们发现约300条重复记录，原因是导入运行了两次。

words.note: 动词 deduplicate（去重），口语 dedupe（读 dee-DOOP）。

words.definition: A field with no value at all in a database.

examples.en: These nulls are customers who didn't give a postcode.
examples.zh: 这些空值是没有填写邮编的客户。

words.note: null 和 0 不一样：null = 没有数据，0 = 数值为零。

words.definition: Show only the data that meets certain conditions; also the control that does this.

examples.en: I've filtered this to show only enterprise customers.
examples.zh: 我把它筛选为只显示企业客户。

examples.en: You can use the filter at the top to pick a region.
examples.zh: 你可以用顶部的筛选器选择地区。

words.note: filter by region = 按地区筛选；filter out = 过滤掉。

words.definition: A group of customers or data that share a characteristic; also the verb for splitting data this way.

examples.en: If we segment by company size, the drop is all in small businesses.
examples.zh: 如果按公司规模细分，下降全部来自小企业。

words.note: 名词重音 SEG-ment，动词可读 seg-MENT。图表里堆积柱的一段也叫 segment。

words.definition: A split of a total into its parts, such as by region or product.

examples.en: Here's the breakdown by region.
examples.zh: 这是按地区的细分。

examples.en: Can we see a breakdown of costs by service?
examples.zh: 能看一下按服务划分的成本明细吗？

words.note: 名词 breakdown 一个词；动词短语 break down（break it down by month 按月拆分）。

words.definition: Move from a summary to more detailed data, such as from year to month to day.

examples.en: If we drill down into March, most of the spike is on one day.
examples.zh: 如果下钻到三月份，大部分峰值集中在一天。

words.note: Power BI / Tableau 里常用；相反方向是 roll up（上卷汇总）。

words.definition: Combine many values into one, such as a sum or average; also the combined total.

examples.en: At an aggregate level things look fine, but two regions are struggling.
examples.zh: 从总体看情况不错，但有两个地区表现不佳。

words.note: 动词读 AG-rih-gate，名词/形容词读 AG-rih-gut。

words.definition: How detailed the data is, such as daily versus monthly.

examples.en: We only have this data at monthly granularity.
examples.zh: 这份数据只有按月的粒度。

words.note: granular data = 细粒度数据。

words.definition: A field you group or slice data by, such as date, region or product.

examples.en: You can switch the dimension from region to product in the drop-down.
examples.zh: 你可以在下拉菜单里把维度从地区切换成产品。

words.definition: A numeric field you calculate, such as total sales or average time.

examples.en: Revenue is a measure; region and month are dimensions.
examples.zh: 收入是度量值，地区和月份是维度。

words.note: Power BI 里叫 measure（度量值），Tableau 里也叫 measures。

words.definition: Rearrange data to summarise it a different way; also to change direction or approach.

examples.en: If we pivot this by month, the seasonality jumps out.
examples.zh: 如果按月透视，季节性就一目了然。

words.definition: Combine two tables using a common field, such as customer ID.

examples.en: I joined the ticket data to the customer table on account ID.
examples.zh: 我按账户ID把工单数据和客户表连接起来。

words.note: inner join、left join 等；口语说 match the two tables up 也可以。

words.definition: A request for specific data from a database, or the code that does it.

examples.en: I'll rerun the query with the latest data after the meeting.
examples.zh: 会后我会用最新数据重新运行查询。

words.definition: A record of the data at one point in time.

examples.en: This is a snapshot as at Monday morning, so it doesn't include this week's orders.
examples.zh: 这是周一早上的快照，所以不包括本周的订单。

words.definition: Update data or a report with the latest values.

examples.en: The dashboard refreshes every night at 2 a.m.
examples.zh: 看板每晚凌晨两点刷新。

words.note: data refresh 失败时可以说 the refresh failed, so the numbers are a day old。

words.definition: How accurate, complete and reliable data is.

examples.en: We have some data quality issues with the older records.
examples.zh: 较早的记录存在一些数据质量问题。

words.definition: The time span the figures cover, such as a month or quarter.

examples.en: The reporting period is 1 July to 30 September.
examples.zh: 报告期为7月1日至9月30日。

words.note: 也说 sample period、period under review。

words.definition: The last date included in the data.

examples.en: The cut-off date was the 25th, so the last few days of the month aren't included.
examples.zh: 截止日期是25号，所以月底最后几天没有包括在内。

words.definition: Used to give the exact date the figures refer to; common in NZ, Australia and the UK.

examples.en: As at 31 March, we had 1,250 active licences.
examples.zh: 截至3月31日，我们有1250个有效许可证。

words.note: 英式/新西兰书面常用 as at；美式更常用 as of。两者都表示“截至”。

words.definition: The exact rule for how a metric is calculated, including what is counted and excluded.

examples.en: Just to be clear on the metric definition: an active user is anyone who logged in during the month.
examples.zh: 先说明一下指标定义：活跃用户是指当月登录过的任何人。

words.note: 中文“口径”可以说 definition 或 how we define / calculate it；“口径不一致”= the definitions don't match。

words.definition: One agreed place where the official version of the data lives.

examples.en: The goal is to make the data warehouse our single source of truth.
examples.zh: 目标是让数据仓库成为我们唯一可信的数据源。

words.note: 缩写 SSOT。

words.definition: A central database that stores data from many systems for reporting and analysis.

examples.en: All these figures come straight from the data warehouse.
examples.zh: 这些数字都直接来自数据仓库。

words.definition: The automated process that moves and transforms data from sources to where it is used.

examples.en: The pipeline failed overnight, so today's numbers are a day behind.
examples.zh: 数据管道昨晚运行失败，所以今天的数字晚了一天。

words.note: ETL = extract, transform, load（抽取、转换、加载）。

words.definition: One piece of information in each record, such as name, date or amount.

examples.en: We don't have a field for industry, so I couldn't break it down that way.
examples.zh: 我们没有行业字段，所以没法按行业细分。

words.note: 在表格里也叫 column（列）；一行叫 row 或 record（记录）。

words.definition: One row in a table, such as one order or one customer.

examples.en: The dataset has about two million records.
examples.zh: 数据集大约有两百万条记录。

words.note: 名词读 REK-ord，动词读 rih-KORD。

words.definition: A file of rows and columns, such as an Excel workbook, used to store and calculate data.

examples.en: I've put the workings in a spreadsheet on SharePoint.
examples.zh: 我把计算过程放在了 SharePoint 上的电子表格里。

words.note: workings = 计算过程（英式）。

words.definition: The date and time recorded when something happened.

examples.en: All timestamps are in UTC, so the daily totals are offset from New Zealand time.
examples.zh: 所有时间戳都是UTC时间，所以每日合计和新西兰时间有偏差。

words.note: 新西兰时间：标准时间 NZST，夏令时 NZDT。按天汇总时要注意时区。

words.definition: Adjust data to a common scale so different groups can be fairly compared.

examples.en: I've normalised by headcount, so it's tickets per employee.
examples.zh: 我按人数做了标准化，所以这是人均工单数。

words.note: 美式拼写 normalize。
