words.definition: Check that two sets of figures match and explain any differences.

examples.en: These numbers reconcile with the finance report to within 1%.
examples.zh: 这些数字与财务报告核对相差不到1%。

words.note: 名词 reconciliation。numbers don't reconcile = 对不上。

words.definition: A quick check that a result is roughly sensible before trusting it.

examples.en: As a sanity check, I compared the total with last month's invoice.
examples.zh: 作为合理性检查，我把总数和上个月的账单对比了一下。

words.definition: Not counting something; often written excl. on slides.

examples.en: All figures are excluding GST.
examples.zh: 所有数字均不含消费税。

words.note: 新西兰常见：excl. GST（不含消费税）/ incl. GST（含消费税）。GST 读 G-S-T。

words.definition: Fill in missing historical data after the fact.

examples.en: We're backfilling the data for August, so that dip will disappear.
examples.zh: 我们正在回填八月的数据，所以那个低谷会消失。

words.definition: The delay between something happening and it showing up in the data.

examples.en: There's a two-day data lag, so the last two days look lower than they really are.
examples.zh: 数据有两天滞后，所以最近两天看起来比实际低。

words.note: incomplete period（不完整的周期）也常要提醒：this month isn't finished yet。

words.definition: Save data out of a system into a file, such as a CSV.

examples.en: I exported the data from Jira into a CSV.
examples.zh: 我把数据从 Jira 导出成了CSV文件。

words.note: 动词重音 ex-PORT，名词 EX-port。CSV 逐个字母读。

words.definition: Break data down in many different ways to look at it from different angles.

examples.en: The dashboard lets you slice and dice the data by team, product and month.
examples.zh: 这个看板让你能按团队、产品和月份多维切分数据。

words.term: I'm going to walk you through
words.definition: A natural way to start a presentation by saying what you will explain step by step.

examples.en: Today I'm going to walk you through last quarter's support numbers.
examples.zh: 今天我来带大家过一遍上季度的支持数据。

words.note: walk someone through = 一步步讲解，比 introduce 更自然。

words.definition: A phrase to introduce context before showing the data.

examples.en: To give you some background, we changed the pricing model in April.
examples.zh: 先介绍一下背景，我们在四月调整了定价模式。

words.definition: A phrase to introduce the first point or chart.

examples.en: Let me start with the big picture, then we'll go region by region.
examples.zh: 我先讲整体情况，然后再逐个地区看。

words.zh: 核心结论是；一句话总结
words.definition: A phrase to give the single most important result first.

examples.en: The headline is that costs are down 12% while usage is up.
examples.zh: 核心结论是：成本下降了12%，而使用量在上升。

words.note: 新西兰/英式职场很常用；也说 the headline number is…

words.definition: A phrase to introduce what a chart is about before explaining details.

examples.en: This chart shows weekly sign-ups over the last six months.
examples.zh: 这张图展示了过去六个月每周的注册量。

words.note: 先说图在讲什么，再说坐标轴，最后说结论，听众更容易跟上。

words.definition: A spoken phrase to point to what is on the slide.

examples.en: Here we have the same data split by region.
examples.zh: 这里是按地区拆分的同一组数据。

words.definition: A phrase to direct the audience to part of the slide.

examples.en: On the left-hand side you can see last year, and on the right-hand side, this year.
examples.zh: 左边是去年，右边是今年。

words.note: 也可简单说 on the left / on the right；at the top / at the bottom。

words.definition: A spoken way to describe what is on the horizontal axis.

examples.en: Along the bottom we have the weeks, and up the side we have the number of tickets.
examples.zh: 横轴是周数，纵轴是工单数量。

words.note: up the side = 纵轴上，口语讲图很自然。

words.definition: A phrase to explain what one mark on a chart stands for.

examples.en: Each dot represents one customer.
examples.zh: 每个点代表一个客户。

words.note: 同样可说 each bar represents… / the blue line represents…

words.definition: A phrase to point out something visible on the slide.

examples.en: As you can see, the line flattens out after June.
examples.zh: 如大家所见，六月之后曲线变平了。

words.note: 不要每句都说，一次演示用两三次就够；也可说 you'll notice that…

words.definition: A phrase to move attention to a particular chart or number.

examples.en: If we look at the mobile numbers, the story is quite different.
examples.zh: 如果我们看一下移动端的数据，情况就很不一样了。

words.definition: A phrase to focus on one part of the data in more detail.

examples.en: Let's zoom in on the last four weeks.
examples.zh: 我们放大看一下最近四周。

words.note: 也说 let's take a closer look at…

words.term: I'd like to draw your attention to
words.definition: A slightly formal phrase to highlight something important.

examples.en: I'd like to draw your attention to the gap in week 32.
examples.zh: 请大家注意第32周的那个缺口。

words.definition: A phrase to highlight the most noticeable finding.

examples.en: What stands out is how quickly the new region has grown.
examples.zh: 最突出的是新地区增长得多快。

words.note: stand out = 突出、显眼。

words.definition: A phrase to state the main point people should remember.

examples.en: The key takeaway is that most of the delay happens before the work even starts.
examples.zh: 最重要的结论是：大部分延误发生在工作开始之前。

words.note: takeaway = 要带走的要点；美式 takeout 是外卖，新西兰外卖叫 takeaway，语境不同。

words.definition: A word to introduce a surprising or notable point.

examples.en: Interestingly, the smallest team has the highest satisfaction score.
examples.zh: 有意思的是，最小的团队满意度得分最高。

words.zh: 放在背景中看；做个对比
words.definition: A phrase to compare a number with something familiar so it makes sense.

examples.en: To put this in context, 200 hours is about one full-time person for six weeks.
examples.zh: 做个对比，200小时大约相当于一个全职员工六周的工作量。

words.note: also: for context, …（作为参考，……）

words.definition: A phrase to explain the same point more simply.

examples.en: In other words, we're spending more to get fewer customers.
examples.zh: 换句话说，我们花得更多，但获得的客户更少。

words.definition: A phrase to show a clear difference between two things.

examples.en: Auckland grew 10%. By contrast, Wellington was flat.
examples.zh: 奥克兰增长了10%。相比之下，惠灵顿持平。

words.note: 也说 in contrast / on the other hand。

words.definition: A word to show that a second point follows the same pattern.

examples.en: Similarly, response times improved in every region.
examples.zh: 同样，每个地区的响应时间都有所改善。

words.definition: A phrase to add a point that slightly contrasts with what you just said.

examples.en: The trend is positive. Having said that, it's only been two months.
examples.zh: 趋势是积极的。话虽如此，毕竟才两个月。

words.note: also: that said、that being said。

words.definition: A phrase to link one point to the next.

examples.en: This brings me to the cost side of the picture.
examples.zh: 这就引出了成本方面的情况。

words.definition: A phrase to change to the next topic or slide.

examples.en: Moving on to customer satisfaction.
examples.zh: 接下来讲客户满意度。

words.note: also: let's move on to… / turning now to…

words.definition: A phrase to show you will return to a point later.

examples.en: There's a reason for that dip, and I'll come back to that in a minute.
examples.zh: 那次回落是有原因的，我稍后再讲。

words.definition: A phrase to return to an earlier slide or point.

examples.en: Let's go back to the previous slide for a second.
examples.zh: 我们回到上一页看一下。

words.definition: What you say when someone else is controlling the slides.

examples.en: Thanks. Next slide, please.
examples.zh: 谢谢。请翻下一页。

words.zh: 大家能看到我的屏幕吗
words.definition: A question to check that screen sharing is working in an online meeting.

examples.en: I'll share my screen. Can everyone see my screen OK?
examples.zh: 我来共享屏幕。大家能正常看到我的屏幕吗？

words.note: 对方回答 Yes, we can see it 或 It's still loading。

words.definition: A phrase to start showing your screen in Teams or Zoom.

examples.en: Let me share my screen and I'll show you the dashboard.
examples.zh: 我来共享屏幕，给大家看一下看板。

words.definition: The overall situation rather than the details.

examples.en: Before we get into the detail, here's the big picture.
examples.zh: 在讲细节之前，先看一下整体情况。

words.definition: A phrase to repeat the main points briefly.

examples.en: To recap, we looked at volume, speed and cost.
examples.zh: 回顾一下，我们看了数量、速度和成本。

words.note: recap 读 REE-kap。

words.definition: A phrase to start your summary at the end.

examples.en: To sum up, we're ahead on revenue but behind on margin.
examples.zh: 总而言之，我们收入领先，但利润率落后。

words.note: also: in summary、to summarise。

words.definition: A phrase to give the most important conclusion, often about money or a decision.

examples.en: The bottom line is we'll need more capacity before Christmas.
examples.zh: 归根结底，圣诞节前我们需要更多容量。

words.note: bottom line 原指损益表最后一行（净利润）。

words.definition: An informal phrase meaning in very few words.

examples.en: In a nutshell, the change worked, but it's expensive to run.
examples.zh: 简而言之，这个改动有效，但运行成本高。

words.zh: 我先停一下，看看大家有没有问题
words.definition: A polite phrase to stop and invite questions.

examples.en: That's the first section. I'll pause there for questions.
examples.zh: 第一部分讲完了。我先停一下，看看大家有没有问题。

words.note: also: Happy to take any questions now。

words.definition: A friendly, common NZ way to finish a presentation.

examples.en: That's all from me. Any questions?
examples.zh: 我就讲到这里。大家有问题吗？

words.definition: Caused mainly by; the most common way to explain a change in a data presentation.

examples.en: The increase was mainly driven by new enterprise customers.
examples.zh: 增长主要由新的企业客户带动。

words.note: 常配 mainly / largely / partly：largely driven by…

words.definition: The biggest cause of a change.

examples.en: The main driver of the cost increase is data storage.
examples.zh: 成本上升的主要驱动因素是数据存储。

words.note: also: a key driver / the biggest contributor。

words.definition: Because of; used after a noun or the verb 'be'.

examples.en: The drop in March is due to the Easter holidays.
examples.zh: 三月份的下降是由于复活节假期。

words.note: 严格语法上 due to 跟在 be 后面（is due to）；句首说 Because of / Owing to 更稳妥。

words.definition: As a result of; the most natural spoken way to give a reason.

examples.en: Response times went up because of the database migration.
examples.zh: 因为数据库迁移，响应时间变长了。

words.definition: Caused by; a formal phrase often used with a percentage.

examples.en: About 60% of the increase is attributable to higher prices.
examples.zh: 约60%的增长可归因于价格上涨。

words.note: 动词 attribute X to Y = 把X归因于Y。

words.definition: Because of something that happened before.

examples.en: As a result of the new process, approvals are 40% faster.
examples.zh: 由于采用了新流程，审批速度提高了40%。

words.definition: Be one of the causes of something.

examples.en: Several factors contributed to the delay.
examples.zh: 有几个因素导致了延误。

words.note: contribute to 表示“部分原因”，不是唯一原因；不要和 cause 混用。名词 contributor。

words.definition: Cause something to happen.

examples.en: The outage led to a spike in support calls.
examples.zh: 故障导致支持来电激增。

words.note: lead-led-led：The change led to…

words.definition: Cause a particular result.

examples.en: Faster onboarding resulted in higher retention.
examples.zh: 更快的上手流程带来了更高的留存率。

words.note: X results in Y（X导致Y）；Y results from X（Y由X导致）。方向别弄反。

words.definition: Come from or be caused by something.

examples.en: Most of the errors stem from one legacy integration.
examples.zh: 大部分错误源于一个老旧的集成。

words.definition: Be balanced or cancelled out by an opposite change.

examples.en: Higher licence costs were offset by savings in hosting.
examples.zh: 许可费的增加被托管费用的节省抵消了。

words.note: partly offset by = 部分抵消。动词 offset 过去式不变。

words.definition: As a result of something positive that happened before.

examples.en: Revenue grew on the back of strong demand from government clients.
examples.zh: 在政府客户强劲需求的推动下，收入增长了。

words.note: 多用于正面结果。

words.definition: Happen at the same time as something else.

examples.en: The dip coincides with the school holidays.
examples.zh: 这次下降与学校假期时间吻合。

words.note: coincide 只说明“同时”，不能证明因果；比 caused by 更谨慎。

words.definition: A phrase to give the reason behind a pattern.

examples.en: Most of the spike can be explained by one large customer onboarding.
examples.zh: 大部分峰值可以用一个大客户入驻来解释。

words.definition: Something that happens only once and is not expected to repeat.

examples.en: The jump in August was a one-off: a large annual payment from one client.
examples.zh: 八月的跳升是一次性的：一个客户支付了大笔年费。

words.note: 形容词 one-off：a one-off cost（一次性成本）。

words.definition: Made to happen by something.

examples.en: The spike was caused by a bot hitting the login page.
examples.zh: 那个峰值是一个机器人反复访问登录页面造成的。

words.definition: Started by a particular event.

examples.en: The alerts were triggered by a misconfigured threshold.
examples.zh: 这些告警是由一个配置错误的阈值触发的。

words.definition: Made stronger or bigger by something.

examples.en: Growth was fuelled by the new partner channel.
examples.zh: 增长由新的合作伙伴渠道推动。

words.note: 美式拼写 fueled。

words.definition: Mostly for the reason that.

examples.en: Costs are lower, largely because we shut down unused servers.
examples.zh: 成本更低，主要是因为我们关闭了闲置的服务器。

words.note: partly because = 部分原因是；mainly because = 主要因为。

words.definition: An indirect effect that one change has on other things.

examples.en: The delay had a knock-on effect on the next two releases.
examples.zh: 这次延误对接下来的两次发布产生了连锁反应。

words.note: 英式/新西兰常用；美式更常说 ripple effect。

words.definition: The effect that something has on something else.

examples.en: We're still measuring the impact on conversion.
examples.zh: 我们还在评估对转化率的影响。

words.note: 名词 have an impact on；动词 impact 也常见（It impacted sales），但有人觉得不够正式，可以用 affect。

words.definition: Connected with, without necessarily saying one causes the other.

examples.en: The drop seems to be linked to the app update.
examples.zh: 这次下降似乎与应用更新有关。

words.definition: The underlying reason a problem happened.

examples.en: We've identified the root cause: a memory leak in the reporting service.
examples.zh: 我们已经找到根本原因：报表服务里有内存泄漏。

words.note: root cause analysis = 根因分析（RCA）。

words.definition: Several causes working together rather than one single reason.

examples.en: It's a combination of factors: price, timing and a competitor launch.
examples.zh: 这是多种因素共同作用：价格、时机和竞争对手的产品发布。

words.definition: Something outside your control that makes progress harder.

examples.en: The exchange rate has been a headwind for our overseas revenue.
examples.zh: 汇率对我们的海外收入一直是个不利因素。

words.definition: Something outside your control that helps progress.

examples.en: The move to remote work was a big tailwind for the product.
examples.zh: 远程办公的趋势对这个产品是很大的利好。

words.definition: Pulled to a lower level by a weak part.

examples.en: The overall score was dragged down by one region.
examples.zh: 整体得分被一个地区拖累了。

words.definition: Increased or helped by something.

examples.en: Sales were boosted by the end-of-year promotion.
examples.zh: 年末促销提振了销售额。

words.definition: After, and often as a result of; used at the start of a phrase.

examples.en: Following the price change, cancellations went up for two weeks.
examples.zh: 价格调整之后，取消量上升了两周。

words.note: following 只说明时间先后，暗示但不断言因果。

words.definition: The overall result after all positive and negative effects are combined.

examples.en: The net effect is a saving of about $8,000 a month.
examples.zh: 综合下来，每月节省约8000元。

words.definition: A warning that a result has limits or conditions.

examples.en: One caveat: this only includes customers who answered the survey.
examples.zh: 需要说明一点：这只包括回复了调查的客户。

words.note: with the caveat that… = 前提是……；I'd add a caveat = 我要补充一个说明。

words.definition: Early and not yet final or fully checked.

examples.en: These are preliminary results, so the numbers may change.
examples.zh: 这些是初步结果，所以数字可能还会变。

words.definition: Not final, and likely to be updated later.

examples.en: September's figures are provisional until finance closes the month.
examples.zh: 九月的数字在财务月结之前都是暂定的。

words.definition: Giving a rough idea rather than an exact or final answer.

examples.en: These costs are indicative only; we'll have firm numbers next week.
examples.zh: 这些成本仅供参考，下周会有确定的数字。

words.zh: 方向性的（看趋势，不看精确值）
words.definition: Showing the general direction of a change, without being precise enough to rely on the exact numbers.

examples.en: Treat this as directional: it tells us which way things are moving, not by how much.
examples.zh: 请把这个当作方向性参考：它告诉我们变化的方向，而不是具体幅度。

words.note: 数据圈常用：directionally correct = 方向上是对的。

words.definition: Too few data points to be fully confident in the result.

examples.en: It's a small sample, only 25 responses, so I'd be careful drawing conclusions.
examples.zh: 样本很小，只有25份回复，所以下结论时要谨慎。

words.term: take this with a pinch of salt
words.definition: An idiom meaning don't fully trust this number.

examples.en: I'd take this with a pinch of salt, because tracking was down for part of the week.
examples.zh: 这个数字要持保留态度，因为那周有段时间埋点出了问题。

words.note: 英式/新西兰说 a pinch of salt；美式说 a grain of salt。

words.definition: It's too soon to judge the final result.

examples.en: It's early days, but the first two weeks look promising.
examples.zh: 现在还早，但前两周的情况看起来不错。

words.definition: There isn't enough time or data yet to reach a conclusion.

examples.en: It's too early to say whether the change has worked.
examples.zh: 现在说这个改动是否有效还太早。

words.note: also: it's too early to tell / too soon to call。

words.definition: A reminder that two things moving together doesn't prove one causes the other.

examples.en: Correlation doesn't imply causation: both could be driven by the busy season.
examples.zh: 相关不等于因果：两者可能都是旺季造成的。

words.note: 口语常简化为 correlation isn't causation。

words.definition: A careful way to state a finding without claiming it is certain.

examples.en: The data suggests that users prefer the shorter form.
examples.zh: 数据表明用户更喜欢简短的表单。

words.note: suggests 比 proves / shows 更谨慎；新西兰职场常用这种语气。

words.definition: A soft way to give an interpretation.

examples.en: It looks like the new process is saving about an hour per request.
examples.zh: 看起来新流程每个请求节省了大约一个小时。

words.note: also: it appears that / it seems that。

words.definition: We can't say that something is impossible or not a factor.

examples.en: We can't rule out that some of the drop is due to the tracking change.
examples.zh: 我们不能排除部分下降是因为埋点调整。

words.definition: Something you accept as true without proof, as a basis for a calculation.

examples.en: The main assumption here is that prices stay the same next year.
examples.zh: 这里的主要假设是明年价格保持不变。

words.note: make an assumption；key assumptions 常单独放一页。

words.definition: A weakness or boundary of the data or method.

examples.en: The main limitation is that we only have data for one region.
examples.zh: 主要的局限性是我们只有一个地区的数据。

words.definition: An unusual situation at the extreme of what is possible, which may behave differently.

examples.en: There are a few edge cases, like customers with two accounts, that I've left out.
examples.zh: 有一些边界情况，比如有两个账户的客户，我没有计算在内。

words.definition: Something that is different from what is normal or expected.

examples.en: The anomaly on the 12th was a data issue, not real usage.
examples.zh: 12号的异常是数据问题，不是真实使用量。

words.note: 形容词 anomalous；anomaly detection = 异常检测。

words.definition: A period or area where data is missing.

examples.en: There's a data gap in early May when the logging was switched off.
examples.zh: 五月初关闭了日志，所以有一段数据缺口。

words.definition: Comparing things on the same basis, so the comparison is fair.

examples.en: On a like-for-like basis, excluding new stores, sales were up 2%.
examples.zh: 按同口径计算（不含新店），销售额增长了2%。

words.note: 英式/新西兰常用；美式说 apples to apples。not like-for-like = 口径不一致，不可直接比较。

words.definition: Remember an important fact when thinking about something.

examples.en: Bear in mind that last year included a one-off project.
examples.zh: 请注意去年包含一个一次性项目。

words.definition: A phrase to point out a fact that affects how to read the data.

examples.en: It's worth noting that this excludes contractors.
examples.zh: 值得注意的是，这不包括合同工。

words.definition: A rough estimate, not an exact number.

examples.en: Just as a ballpark figure, we're talking about $50,000.
examples.zh: 只是个大概数字，大约是5万元。

words.note: also: in the ballpark（大致在这个范围）。

words.definition: Done quickly and roughly, not with full analysis.

examples.en: This is a back-of-the-envelope calculation, but it shows the scale of the problem.
examples.zh: 这只是粗略估算，但能说明问题的规模。

words.definition: Not final, and may be changed later.

examples.en: All dates on this slide are subject to change.
examples.zh: 这页上的所有日期都可能变动。

words.definition: At the current point in time, implying things may change.

examples.en: At this stage, we don't know how many users are affected.
examples.zh: 目前我们还不知道有多少用户受影响。

words.definition: A plain way to say a conclusion isn't possible yet.

examples.en: We don't have enough data to break it down by region yet.
examples.zh: 我们的数据还不够，暂时没法按地区细分。

words.definition: Possibly, but not certainly.

examples.en: This could potentially save us 20 hours a month.
examples.zh: 这可能每月为我们节省20个小时。

words.definition: The most likely answer based on what you know, admitted to be uncertain.

examples.en: My best guess is that it'll level off at around 60%.
examples.zh: 我的最佳估计是它会在60%左右趋于平稳。

words.definition: Made unrepresentative because of one unusual value or group.

examples.en: The average is skewed by one very large order.
examples.zh: 平均值被一笔超大订单拉偏了。

words.definition: Not very sure about a number or conclusion.

examples.en: I'd say we have low confidence in the Q4 forecast.
examples.zh: 我们对第四季度预测的把握不大。

words.note: 反义 high confidence。I'm fairly confident that… = 我比较有把握……

words.definition: A problem that has already been identified but not yet fixed.

examples.en: The duplicate counts in this report are a known issue and will be fixed next sprint.
examples.zh: 这份报告中的重复计数是已知问题，下个迭代会修复。

words.definition: Caused by things the team cannot influence.

examples.en: Some of the delay was outside our control, such as the vendor outage.
examples.zh: 部分延误是我们无法控制的，比如供应商的故障。

words.definition: A clear phrase to give your main recommendation.

examples.en: We recommend moving the remaining servers to reserved instances.
examples.zh: 我们建议把剩余的服务器改为预留实例。

words.note: recommend + doing 或 recommend that we do；不说 recommend to do。

words.definition: A softer, more personal way to make a recommendation.

examples.en: I'd suggest we run the test for another two weeks before deciding.
examples.zh: 我建议再测试两周再做决定。

words.note: suggest + that 从句或 doing；不说 suggest you to do。

words.definition: A phrase to say what should happen next.

examples.en: The next step is to validate these numbers with the finance team.
examples.zh: 下一步是和财务团队核实这些数字。

words.definition: Interesting or important enough to look into further.

examples.en: The drop in mobile conversion is worth investigating.
examples.zh: 移动端转化率的下降值得研究一下。

words.note: also: worth looking into / worth exploring。

words.definition: Look at something in more detail to understand it better.

examples.en: We'll dig deeper into the churned accounts next week.
examples.zh: 下周我们会深入分析流失的账户。

words.note: also: dig into the data。

words.definition: A detailed analysis of one specific topic.

examples.en: I'll do a deep dive on the Christchurch numbers for next month's meeting.
examples.zh: 下个月的会议我会对基督城的数据做一次深度分析。

words.definition: A specific task agreed in a meeting, with an owner and a deadline.

examples.en: So the action item for me is to rerun the analysis with the new definition.
examples.zh: 那我的待办事项是用新定义重新做一遍分析。

words.note: also: action point（英式）、AP。

words.definition: The person responsible for a task or metric.

examples.en: Who's the owner for this one?
examples.zh: 这件事谁负责？

words.note: 动词 own：Can you own this? = 这个你能负责吗？

words.definition: A change that is easy to make and gives a fast, visible benefit.

examples.en: Turning off idle dev environments at night is a quick win.
examples.zh: 晚上关闭闲置的开发环境是一个快速见效的措施。

words.definition: The easiest problems to fix or gains to get first.

examples.en: We've already picked the low-hanging fruit, so the next savings will be harder.
examples.zh: 容易的部分我们已经做完了，接下来的节省会更难。

words.definition: A balance between two things you can't fully have at the same time.

examples.en: There's a trade-off between cost and speed here.
examples.zh: 这里需要在成本和速度之间取舍。

words.note: 动词短语 trade off（不带连字符）。

words.definition: Decide which things are most important and do them first.

examples.en: I'd prioritise the top three error types, since they cause 80% of the tickets.
examples.zh: 我会优先处理前三种错误类型，因为它们造成了80%的工单。

words.note: 美式拼写 prioritize；名词 priority。

words.definition: Decide to give less importance or time to something.

examples.en: We'd deprioritise the reporting features until the migration is done.
examples.zh: 在迁移完成之前，我们会把报表功能的优先级降低。

words.definition: Watch something carefully over time.

examples.en: We'll monitor the error rate for the next two weeks.
examples.zh: 接下来两周我们会持续监控错误率。

words.definition: An informal phrase for watching something.

examples.en: Let's keep an eye on churn over the next couple of months.
examples.zh: 接下来几个月我们留意一下流失率。

words.definition: Look at a topic or decision again later.

examples.en: Let's revisit this in a month, when we have more data.
examples.zh: 一个月后数据更多时我们再来看这个。

words.definition: Take further action or get more information after a meeting.

examples.en: I'll follow up with the infrastructure team about the storage costs.
examples.zh: 我会就存储成本跟基础设施团队跟进。

words.note: 名词 follow-up（带连字符）：a follow-up meeting。

words.definition: A small trial before a full rollout; also a verb.

examples.en: We'd like to pilot this with one team before rolling it out.
examples.zh: 我们想先在一个团队试点，再全面推广。

words.note: 名词：run a pilot；形容词：a pilot project。

words.definition: Introduce something to everyone, often in stages.

examples.en: If the pilot works, we'll roll it out to all regions in Q2.
examples.zh: 如果试点成功，我们会在第二季度推广到所有地区。

words.note: 名词 rollout（一个词）。

words.definition: Make something bigger, such as a successful trial.

examples.en: The results are good enough to scale up.
examples.zh: 结果足够好，可以扩大规模了。

words.note: 反义 scale back / scale down（缩小规模）。

words.definition: Put even more effort or money into something that is working.

examples.en: Given these results, I think we should double down on the partner channel.
examples.zh: 鉴于这些结果，我认为我们应该加大对合作渠道的投入。

words.definition: From now on, in the future.

examples.en: Going forward, we'll report this metric weekly.
examples.zh: 今后我们会每周报告这个指标。

words.note: 商务口语非常常见；also: moving forward。

words.definition: The different choices available.

examples.en: We see three options, and I'll go through the pros and cons of each.
examples.zh: 我们有三个方案，我会逐一说明利弊。

words.note: pros and cons = 利弊（读 prohz and konz）。

words.definition: Comparing what something costs with what you gain from it.

examples.en: We'd need a proper cost-benefit analysis before committing.
examples.zh: 在做决定之前，我们需要做一个正式的成本效益分析。

words.definition: In the near future.

examples.en: In the short term, we can add more staff; in the long term, we need automation.
examples.zh: 短期内可以增加人手；长期来看，我们需要自动化。

words.note: in the long term = 长期来看；in the medium term = 中期。

words.definition: Give official approval.

examples.en: We need the steering group to sign off on the budget.
examples.zh: 我们需要指导小组批准预算。

words.note: 名词 sign-off：We have sign-off from finance。

words.definition: An approach of trying small changes, measuring results and adjusting.

examples.en: I'd take a test-and-learn approach rather than changing everything at once.
examples.zh: 我建议采取边试边学的方法，而不是一次性全改。

words.definition: Decide on a number you want to reach.

examples.en: I'd suggest we set a target of under 2% churn by the end of the year.
examples.zh: 我建议设定一个年底流失率低于2%的目标。

words.definition: A friendly way to start answering a question and give yourself a moment to think.

examples.en: Good question. The short answer is yes, but it depends on the region.
examples.zh: 好问题。简短回答是：是的，但要看地区。

words.note: 不要每个问题都说，以免显得敷衍；也可以说 That's a great point。

words.term: let me check and get back to you
words.definition: A polite way to say you don't know yet and will answer later.

examples.en: I don't want to guess, so let me check and get back to you.
examples.zh: 我不想乱猜，我查一下再回复你。

words.note: 不知道时这样回答很专业，比硬答更好。

words.term: I don't have that number to hand
words.definition: A polite way to say you don't have the figure with you right now.

examples.en: I don't have that number to hand, but I can send it after the meeting.
examples.zh: 我手头没有那个数字，会后发给你。

words.note: 英式/新西兰说 to hand，美式说 on hand / handy。

words.term: off the top of my head
words.definition: Without checking, from memory, so the answer may not be exact.

examples.en: Off the top of my head, it's about 40%, but I'll confirm.
examples.zh: 凭印象大概40%，我会再确认一下。

words.term: that's outside the scope of this analysis
words.zh: 那不在这次分析的范围内
words.definition: A polite way to say a question is not covered by the work.

examples.en: That's outside the scope of this analysis, but it would be a good follow-up.
examples.zh: 那不在这次分析的范围内，但可以作为后续研究。

words.definition: A phrase to check or explain something so there is no confusion.

examples.en: Just to clarify, are we talking about new customers or all customers?
examples.zh: 确认一下，我们说的是新客户还是所有客户？

words.definition: A phrase to check what the question means before answering.

examples.en: Are you asking about this year only, or compared with last year?
examples.zh: 你是只问今年，还是和去年相比？

words.definition: A phrase to repeat the question in your own words to check it.

examples.en: If I understand correctly, you want to know why March is higher.
examples.zh: 如果我理解得没错，你想知道为什么三月份更高。

words.term: could you say a bit more
words.definition: A polite request for more detail about a question.

examples.en: Could you say a bit more about what you mean by efficiency?
examples.zh: 你说的效率具体指什么，能再说说吗？

words.note: also: Could you expand on that?

words.definition: A phrase to move a detailed or off-topic discussion to after the meeting.

examples.en: That's quite a detailed one, so I'll take that offline with you.
examples.zh: 这个问题比较细，我们会后单独聊吧。

words.note: offline 在这里不是“断网”，而是“会后私下”。

words.definition: A phrase to give a quick, simple answer before any detail.

examples.en: The short answer is no; the long answer is that it depends on the contract.
examples.zh: 简短回答是不会；详细说的话，要看合同。

words.definition: A polite way to agree that someone's challenge is reasonable.

examples.en: That's a fair point. The sample does lean towards larger customers.
examples.zh: 说得有道理。样本确实偏向大客户。

words.definition: A phrase to accept part of someone's point before adding your own view.

examples.en: You're right that the numbers are small, but the trend is consistent.
examples.zh: 你说得对，数字确实不大，但趋势是一致的。

words.definition: A phrase to show you already considered something.

examples.en: We did look into that, and seasonality only explains about a third of the change.
examples.zh: 我们确实研究过，季节性只能解释大约三分之一的变化。

words.term: we haven't looked at that yet
words.definition: An honest phrase to say an area hasn't been analysed.

examples.en: We haven't looked at that yet, but it's a good idea for the next round.
examples.zh: 我们还没研究过这个，但这是下一轮的好方向。

words.definition: A phrase to say you will find and show something on screen.

examples.en: Let me pull that up on the dashboard.
examples.zh: 我在看板上调出来看一下。

words.definition: A phrase to say you are not fully sure and need to confirm.

examples.en: I think it's around 300, but I'd have to double-check.
examples.zh: 我觉得大约300，但我得再核实一下。

words.definition: A phrase to explain that the answer changes with conditions.

examples.en: It depends on how we define an active user.
examples.zh: 这要看我们怎么定义活跃用户。

words.zh: 这样回答了你的问题吗
words.definition: A phrase to check that the person is satisfied with your answer.

examples.en: Does that answer your question, or would you like more detail?
examples.zh: 这样回答了你的问题吗？还是需要更多细节？

words.note: also: Does that make sense? / Does that help?

words.term: happy to go into more detail
words.definition: A friendly offer to explain further if people want.

examples.en: I'm happy to go into more detail on the method if that's useful.
examples.zh: 如果有用的话，我可以再详细讲讲方法。

words.term: can I come back to that at the end
words.zh: 我可以最后再回答这个吗
words.definition: A polite way to delay a question until later in the presentation.

examples.en: Can I come back to that at the end? It's covered on a later slide.
examples.zh: 我可以最后再回答吗？后面有一页会讲到。

words.definition: A phrase to promise a written answer after the meeting.

examples.en: I'll follow up by email with the full breakdown.
examples.zh: 我会后发邮件把完整的明细发给大家。

words.definition: A phrase to invite more questions before finishing.

examples.en: Any other questions before we wrap up?
examples.zh: 结束之前还有其他问题吗？

words.note: wrap up = 收尾、结束会议。

words.zh: 接着这个话题；补充一下
words.definition: A phrase to add to what someone else has just said.

examples.en: To build on that, we also saw the same pattern in the survey results.
examples.zh: 补充一下，我们在调查结果里也看到了同样的规律。
